Univariate G-study: Mental Health

Generalizability Theory for LLM-as-Evaluator Reliability

Liu, J. and Perera, R. A.

07 September 2026

Supportive analysis from the earlier R1 lme4 workflow. The primary revised estimates are in the paired OpenMx report. Original analysis code and numerical outputs are retained here.

Reproducing this report

# What this render does is set by its parameters.  The statement below is
# generated from them rather than asserted, and the provenance block at the end
# records what was reloaded and what was computed once the document has run.
RENDER_SCOPE <- local({
  boot_stage <- identical(params$stage, "bootstrap")
  rc <- isTRUE(params$reuse_comparison)
  rb <- isTRUE(params$reuse_bootstrap)
  comp <- if (rc) paste("the model comparison and the REML refits are reloaded from an earlier render of this document",
                        "when its saved tables are present (fitted here when they are absent); a saved comparison that",
                        "fails the fingerprint check stops the render instead of being refitted silently (a pre-fingerprint",
                        "table is accepted only when `reuse_from` names it explicitly)")
          else "every specification is fitted and the reported specification is refitted in this render"
  boot <- if (!boot_stage) "no bootstrap is run, so no bootstrap intervals appear"
          else if (rb) paste("the bootstrap replicates are reloaded from the cache where it passes the fingerprint,",
                             "version and layout checks, and recomputed otherwise")
          else "the bootstrap is computed in this render"
  head <- sprintf("This render was requested with `stage = \"%s\"`, `reuse_comparison = %s` and `reuse_bootstrap = %s`: %s; %s.",
                  params$stage, rc, rb, comp, boot)
  tail <- if (boot_stage && !rc && !rb)
    "That is the complete report: each chunk shows its code together with the output it produced here."
  else paste("Where a result is reloaded, the chunk concerned prints a \"loaded\" note in place of its fitting output;",
             "the provenance block at the end records what was reloaded and what was computed.")
  paste(head, tail)
})

This render was requested with stage = "bootstrap", reuse_comparison = FALSE and reuse_bootstrap = FALSE: every specification is fitted and the reported specification is refitted in this render; the bootstrap is computed in this render. That is the complete report: each chunk shows its code together with the output it produced here. The source .Rmd is embedded (Code menu, top right, “Download Rmd”). To reproduce the complete report from the source data:

# From the folder holding this .Rmd, with the data files in ../../data (see "Inputs" below).
rmarkdown::render("uni_mental_health.Rmd",
  params = list(stage = "bootstrap", B_boot = 1000, benchmarks = TRUE,
                reuse_comparison = FALSE, reuse_bootstrap = FALSE,
                boot_cores = 4))          # or use run_all_rmd.R with MG_STAGE=bootstrap MG_BENCHMARKS=true MG_REUSE_COMPARISON=false

The source defaults (stage = "models", benchmarks = false) render the point-estimate document in 30–90 minutes; the command above is the full report and takes roughly 10–25 hours per document on 2–4 cores, almost all of it the 1,000 item-cluster refits plus the 100-fold jackknife. Two switches trade completeness for time and are meant for checking wording, not for the deliverable: reuse_comparison = TRUE reloads the model comparison and REML refits written by an earlier render of this document (accepted only if the data, specification set, seed and optimizer settings match; otherwise the render stops and asks for reuse_comparison = FALSE; the one exception is a table written before the fingerprint columns existed, which is accepted only when reuse_from names its directory explicitly, and the provenance block then says so), and reuse_bootstrap = TRUE reloads the bootstrap replicates from the cache the bootstrap stage writes (accepted only if the fingerprint, computation version, replicate count and statistic layout match). Where a switch is on, the corresponding chunk prints a “loaded” note instead of its fitting output.

Where the manuscript tables come from in this report: Table 2 (variance components) from Refit with REML; Table 3 (coefficients with Wald and bootstrap intervals) from that section and from D-study with bootstrap intervals; Table 4 (D-study projections and intervals) from D-study with bootstrap intervals; Supplementary S13 (entropy strata) and S5 (scoring order) from Scale and sample sensitivities, both truncated method-of-moments; S3 from Model definitions and sensitivity comparison; S9 from Facet severity with item-clustered inference; S6–S8 from Signed variance decomposition.

Revision history. A complete render on 2026-09-05 was followed on 2026-09-06 by in-place corrections of explanatory text only (the estimator-term wording in The item component against the ANOVA value, the caption of the naive-versus-clustered significance table, the OSF link, and the supplementary table numbers above). On 2026-09-06 Family 1 (now 1E) was redefined so that every facet outside the instrument is a nested replication (prompt, temperature and seed within the evaluator; three members mirroring Family 2 without the shared prompt effects), the family set was widened to every member (eleven after Family 1P, the prompt as the instrument and the mirror of 1E, was added on 2026-09-07), and the third-member label changed from drift to temperature interaction; the provenance statement at the top of this document records what the present render fitted and what, if anything, it reloaded.

This document is self-contained: every function it uses is defined below, so it can be knitted on its own with no other file from the repository apart from the source data, covering both label scorings.

What it contains depends on params$stage, and the heading below says which. The models stage runs the signed variance decomposition, the model-sensitivity comparison, the REML refit of the reported specification, and the D-study projections — all point estimates, no resampling. The bootstrap stage runs all of that and then refits the reported specification on item-cluster resamples, attaches BCa intervals to the projections, and runs the facet-severity models with item-clustered inference, so one render in the bootstrap stage is the complete document. B_boot is a configured parameter in both; it is only spent in the second.

The seven-level scoring (7L) and the three-level collapse (3L) are two mappings of the same 21,600 annotations of the same 100 items. Every table below therefore carries a scoring column and reports both, which makes the comparison between them structural rather than a separate exercise: how the variance partition and the coefficients move when the scale is coarsened is itself the evidence bearing on whether the ordinal mapping drives the conclusions.

Companion documents cover the other tasks (uni_drug_review.Rmd, uni_hate_speech.Rmd) and the multivariate analyses (mv_*.Rmd).

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(lme4)      # mixed-model fits
  library(dplyr)     # data assembly
  library(numDeriv)  # Hessian / gradient for the delta-method Wald intervals
  library(MASS)      # polr(), cumulative logit facet-severity models
})

SCORINGS <- c("7L", "3L")
DATASET_OF <- c("7L" = "mental_health_7L", "3L" = "mental_health_3L")
DATA_DIR <- normalizePath(params$data_dir, mustWork = TRUE)
OUT_DIR  <- params$out_dir
BOOT_REUSED <- list()   # per bootstrap cache key: TRUE if reloaded, FALSE if computed here
SEV_REUSED  <- list()   # the same for the facet-severity replicates
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
OUT_DIR  <- normalizePath(OUT_DIR)

# Defined here rather than inside the bootstrap chunk: the provenance block
# references it in both stages, so it cannot live inside a bootstrap-only chunk.
B_BOOT      <- params$B_boot
if (identical(params$stage, "bootstrap") && B_BOOT < 1)
  stop("B_boot must be at least 1 in the bootstrap stage (the facet-severity bootstrap has no zero-draw path); ",
       "use stage = 'models' to skip the bootstrap")
set.seed(params$seed)

1 The design

The Mental-Health annotation grid is a fully crossed, fully balanced five-way design: 100 items are each evaluated by every combination of 4 evaluators, 3 prompt types, 6 temperatures and 3 seeds, giving 21,600 observations. Items are the object of measurement. An evaluator–prompt pair defines an instrument configuration; temperature varies the protocol within a configuration, and seed provides replication. The 12 configurations are crossed but not treated as independent instruments because configurations sharing an evaluator or prompt also share structure. Both scorings use this same design.

# One name for the estimator, used everywhere the string appears: in the
# exported `estimator` column, in captions, and in the provenance block.  A
# single constant keeps them in step; literal estimator strings scattered
# across the document are the failure mode it prevents.
COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR <- toupper(params$comparison_estimator)
REPORT_ESTIMATOR    <- toupper(params$report_estimator)
if (!identical(REPORT_ESTIMATOR, "REML")) stop("report_estimator must be \"REML\": the sensitivity refits are REML and every reported label assumes it")
if (!COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR %in% c("REML", "ML")) stop('comparison_estimator must be "REML" or "ML"')
if (!REPORT_ESTIMATOR %in% c("REML", "ML")) stop('report_estimator must be "REML" or "ML"')
USE_REML_COMPARE <- identical(COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR, "REML")
USE_REML_REPORT <- identical(REPORT_ESTIMATOR, "REML")

# Retain ESTIMATOR/USE_REML as the report-side labels expected downstream.
ESTIMATOR <- REPORT_ESTIMATOR
USE_REML  <- USE_REML_REPORT

# score ~ 1 in every specification, so one fixed effect throughout.  Used by the
# information criteria: under REML the intercept is not counted and the penalty
# is over n - p; under ML it is counted and the penalty is over n.
P_FIX <- 1L

FACETS <- c("item", "evaluator", "prompt", "temp", "seed")
OBJECT <- "item"
SHORT  <- c(item = "i", evaluator = "e", prompt = "p", temp = "t", seed = "s")
DSIZE  <- c(item = 100, evaluator = 4, prompt = 3, temp = 6, seed = 3)

# The observed design, used whenever a coefficient is reported "as measured".
# Derived from DSIZE rather than retyped: two independent copies of the same
# numbers is how a silent mismatch with the data gets in.
DESIGN <- as.list(setNames(as.numeric(DSIZE[c("evaluator", "prompt", "temp", "seed")]),
                           c("e", "p", "t", "s")))

1.1 Loading the outcome, under both scorings

G-theory needs a numeric outcome, so the categorical labels are mapped to ordinal severity scores. Two mappings are used, unchanged from the original analysis. The seven-level scoring keeps every category distinct; the three-level collapse groups them into non-clinical, internalising, and high-acuity bands.

The step deserves scrutiny: whether categories such as anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder and personality disorder sit on a common severity dimension at all is a real question, not a technicality. Carrying both scorings through every analysis is how it gets answered with numbers — if the partition and the coefficients are stable across a coarsening this severe, the conclusions do not rest on the particular values assigned.

MH7 <- c(NORMAL = 1, STRESS = 2, ANXIETY = 3, DEPRESSION = 4,
         BIPOLAR = 5, PERSONALITY_DISORDER = 6, SUICIDAL = 7)
MH3 <- c(NORMAL = 1, STRESS = 1, ANXIETY = 2, DEPRESSION = 2,
         BIPOLAR = 3, PERSONALITY_DISORDER = 3, SUICIDAL = 3)
MAPS <- list("7L" = MH7, "3L" = MH3)

#' Load the Mental-Health outcome in long form under standard facet names,
#' scored by the supplied label map.
load_mental_health <- function(data_dir, map) {
  d <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "mh_labeling_final.csv"),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  score <- as.numeric(map[d$label])
  if (any(is.na(score))) stop("unmapped labels in mental_health")
  data.frame(
    score     = score,
    item      = factor(d$item_id),
    evaluator = factor(d$evaluator),
    prompt    = factor(d$prompt_type),
    temp      = factor(d$temperature),
    seed      = factor(d$seed),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# One frame per scoring.  Both are held for the whole document; every analysis
# chunk below iterates over SCORINGS and labels its rows accordingly.
DS <- lapply(MAPS, function(m) load_mental_health(DATA_DIR, m))

#' Reshape a complete balanced long frame into a five-way array with facets
#' on axes in FACETS order (item first). Errors rather than silently filling
#' if the design is not complete and balanced.
to_array <- function(df, score_col = "score") {
  levs <- lapply(FACETS, function(f) sort(unique(df[[f]])))
  names(levs) <- FACETS
  dims <- vapply(levs, length, integer(1))
  idx  <- vapply(FACETS, function(f) match(df[[f]], levs[[f]]),
                 integer(nrow(df)))
  lin  <- idx[, 1]
  mult <- 1
  for (j in seq_along(FACETS)[-1]) {
    mult <- mult * dims[j - 1]
    lin  <- lin + (idx[, j] - 1) * mult
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(lin))          stop("duplicate factor combinations")
  if (length(lin) != prod(dims))   stop("design is not complete/balanced")
  arr <- array(NA_real_, dim = unname(dims))
  arr[lin] <- df[[score_col]]
  if (anyNA(arr))                  stop("design is not complete/balanced")
  arr
}

ARR <- lapply(DS, to_array)

# DSIZE and DESIGN are asserted against the data, not trusted.  Every
# method-of-moments coefficient and every "observed design" projection divides
# by these numbers; if the source CSV ever changed shape, both would be
# silently wrong rather than loudly absent.
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  stopifnot(identical(dim(ARR[[sc]]), unname(as.integer(DSIZE))))
  cat(sprintf("%-3s array dimensions: %s - matches the declared design\n",
              sc, paste(dim(ARR[[sc]]), collapse = " x ")))
}
#> 7L  array dimensions: 100 x 4 x 3 x 6 x 3 - matches the declared design
#> 3L  array dimensions: 100 x 4 x 3 x 6 x 3 - matches the declared design

2 Signed variance decomposition

Why the signed decomposition is reported alongside the likelihood fits.

The original analysis estimated variance components with a likelihood-based mixed model, which constrains every variance to be non-negative and therefore reports near-zero facets as exactly zero. A boundary estimate is not by itself evidence that a component is truly zero, and the alternatives carry different implications: a component can be pushed to the boundary by sampling variability, by a large higher-order interaction, or by a misspecified covariance structure.

Because this design is balanced, the classical ANOVA / method-of-moments estimators apply directly and are equivalent to GENOVA’s. They impose no non-negativity constraint, so the sign and magnitude of every component survive — which is the diagnostic being asked for. The decomposition is exact algebra on the sums of squares and depends on no model fit at all, partitioning the design into all \(2^5 - 1 = 31\) components.

.all_subsets <- function(k) {
  out <- list()
  for (r in seq_len(k)) out <- c(out, combn(k, r, simplify = FALSE))
  out
}
.key <- function(A) paste(A, collapse = ",")

# Proper subsets of a set, by POSITION. combn() coerces a length-1 first
# argument to seq_len(), so combn(A, r) on a singleton silently enumerates
# 1..A instead of A itself; indexing through seq_along(A) avoids that.
.subsets_of <- function(A, r) {
  lapply(combn(seq_along(A), r, simplify = FALSE), function(ii) A[ii])
}

#' Exact expected-mean-squares variance components for a balanced fully
#' crossed array. Returns a named numeric vector of SIGNED components keyed
#' by facet-name interaction (e.g. "item:evaluator"), with mean squares,
#' degrees of freedom and facet sets attached as attributes.
variance_components <- function(arr, names_ = FACETS) {
  dims <- dim(arr); k <- length(dims); N <- length(arr)
  subs <- .all_subsets(k)

  # "@" keys the empty set; R environments reject zero-length names.
  U <- new.env(hash = TRUE, parent = emptyenv())
  assign("@", sum(arr)^2 / N, envir = U)
  for (S in subs) {
    tot <- apply(arr, S, sum)
    assign(.key(S), sum(tot^2) / (N / length(tot)), envir = U)
  }

  MS <- numeric(length(subs)); DF <- numeric(length(subs))
  nm <- character(length(subs))
  for (i in seq_along(subs)) {
    A  <- subs[[i]]
    ss <- ((-1)^length(A)) * get("@", envir = U)
    for (r in seq_len(length(A))) {
      for (B in .subsets_of(A, r)) {
        ss <- ss + ((-1)^(length(A) - r)) * get(.key(B), envir = U)
      }
    }
    DF[i] <- prod(dims[A] - 1)
    MS[i] <- ss / DF[i]
    nm[i] <- .key(A)
  }
  names(MS) <- nm; names(DF) <- nm

  ord     <- order(vapply(subs, length, integer(1)), decreasing = TRUE)
  sig2    <- numeric(0)
  setlist <- list()
  for (i in ord) {
    A <- subs[[i]]; kA <- .key(A)
    adj <- 0
    for (tk in names(sig2)) {
      Tv <- setlist[[tk]]
      if (length(Tv) > length(A) && all(A %in% Tv)) {
        adj <- adj + (N / prod(dims[Tv])) * sig2[[tk]]
      }
    }
    sig2[kA]     <- (MS[[kA]] - adj) / (N / prod(dims[A]))
    setlist[[kA]] <- A
  }

  pretty <- vapply(names(sig2), function(kk) {
    paste(names_[as.integer(strsplit(kk, ",")[[1]])], collapse = ":")
  }, character(1))
  out <- as.numeric(sig2); names(out) <- pretty
  attr(out, "MS")   <- MS[names(sig2)]
  attr(out, "DF")   <- DF[names(sig2)]
  attr(out, "sets") <- setlist[names(sig2)]
  out
}
#' Erho2 / Phi at a projected design from a full-crossed component vector.
#' n is a named vector giving the number of levels of each NON-object facet.
#' truncate = FALSE keeps negative components, which is what makes the
#' signed-vs-truncated comparison below meaningful.
g_coefficients <- function(vc, n, truncate = TRUE) {
  tau <- 0; rel <- 0; abso <- 0
  for (i in seq_along(vc)) {
    v <- vc[[i]]
    if (truncate && v < 0) v <- 0
    parts  <- strsplit(names(vc)[i], ":")[[1]]
    others <- setdiff(parts, OBJECT)
    denom  <- if (length(others)) prod(n[others]) else 1
    if (OBJECT %in% parts) {
      if (!length(others)) tau <- tau + v
      else { rel <- rel + v / denom; abso <- abso + v / denom }
    } else {
      abso <- abso + v / denom
    }
  }
  c(tau = tau, rel_error_var = rel, abs_error_var = abso,
    Erho2 = tau / (tau + rel), Phi = tau / (tau + abso))
}

2.1 Solving, with an algebraic self-check

The mean squares must rebuild the total corrected sum of squares exactly. A silent failure here would invalidate every component below, so this is an assertion rather than a logged diagnostic.

VC <- list(); id_rows <- list()

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  a  <- ARR[[sc]]
  vc <- variance_components(a)
  VC[[sc]] <- vc
  MS <- attr(vc, "MS"); DF <- attr(vc, "DF")

  ss_direct <- sum((a - mean(a))^2)
  ss_from   <- sum(MS * DF)
  if (abs(ss_direct - ss_from) > 1e-6 * ss_direct) {
    stop(sprintf("SS identity failed for %s: %.6f vs %.6f",
                 sc, ss_direct, ss_from))
  }

  # A second, stronger identity: the SS check verifies that the mean squares
  # partition the total, this verifies that the top-down back-solve inverted the
  # expectation correctly.  Two keying schemes coexist -- `vc` by effect name,
  # MS/DF/sets by the solver's index key, same order -- so the loop matches them
  # BY POSITION, and `sets` holds positions in FACETS so DIMS is indexed
  # positionally too.
  SETS <- attr(vc, "sets"); DIMS <- dim(a); N_CELL <- prod(DIMS)
  stopifnot(length(MS) == length(vc), length(SETS) == length(vc))
  ems_max_rel <- 0
  for (ia in seq_along(MS)) {
    Aset <- SETS[[ia]]; pred <- 0
    for (it in seq_along(vc)) {
      Tset <- SETS[[it]]
      if (all(Aset %in% Tset)) pred <- pred + (N_CELL / prod(DIMS[Tset])) * vc[[it]]
    }
    ems_max_rel <- max(ems_max_rel, abs(pred - MS[[ia]]) / max(abs(MS[[ia]]), 1e-12))
  }
  if (ems_max_rel > 1e-8)
    stop(sprintf("EMS back-solve identity failed for %s: max relative error %.3e",
                 sc, ems_max_rel))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] EMS back-solve identity: max relative error %.3e over %d terms\n",
              sc, ems_max_rel, length(MS)))

  # Both identities exported, not just the weaker one; see the other univariate
  # documents.
  id_rows[[sc]] <- data.frame(
    dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc,
    check   = c("corrected_SS_reconstruction", "EMS_backsolve_identity"),
    direct  = c(ss_direct, NA_real_),
    from_mean_squares = c(ss_from, NA_real_),
    abs_diff = c(abs(ss_direct - ss_from), NA_real_),
    max_rel_error = c(NA_real_, ems_max_rel),
    n_terms = c(NA_integer_, length(MS)),
    row.names = NULL)

  cat(sprintf("%-3s SS identity holds: direct = %.6f, from mean squares = %.6f (diff %.3e)\n",
              sc, ss_direct, ss_from, abs(ss_direct - ss_from)))
}
#> [7L] EMS back-solve identity: max relative error 1.570e-16 over 31 terms
#> 7L  SS identity holds: direct = 105033.419259, from mean squares = 105033.419259 (diff 1.055e-08)
#> [3L] EMS back-solve identity: max relative error 1.638e-16 over 31 terms
#> 3L  SS identity holds: direct = 13233.953287, from mean squares = 13233.953287 (diff 2.710e-10)
identity_check <- do.call(rbind, id_rows)

2.2 The 31 components

The table lists all 31 signed components. Which term of a specification absorbs each of them is classified in the section What each specification absorbs, once the specifications have been defined.

COMP <- list(); TOT_TR <- list()

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  vc <- VC[[sc]]
  MS <- attr(vc, "MS"); DF <- attr(vc, "DF")
  tot_tr  <- sum(pmax(vc, 0))
  parts_l <- lapply(names(vc), function(x) strsplit(x, ":")[[1]])

  cp <- data.frame(
    dataset       = DATASET_OF[[sc]],
    scoring       = sc,
    effect        = names(vc),
    effect_short  = vapply(parts_l, function(p) paste(SHORT[p], collapse = ""),
                           character(1)),
    order         = vapply(parts_l, length, integer(1)),
    df            = as.numeric(DF),
    mean_square   = as.numeric(MS),
    var_signed    = as.numeric(vc),
    var_truncated = pmax(as.numeric(vc), 0),
    is_negative   = as.numeric(vc) < 0,
    row.names = NULL)
  cp$pct_of_total_truncated <- 100 * cp$var_truncated / tot_tr
  COMP[[sc]]   <- cp[order(-cp$var_truncated), ]
  TOT_TR[[sc]] <- tot_tr
}
comp <- do.call(rbind, COMP)

# Side by side: the same 31 effects, ranked under each scoring.
side <- merge(
  COMP[["7L"]][, c("effect_short", "order", "var_truncated", "pct_of_total_truncated")],

  by = "effect_short", suffixes = c("_7L", "_3L"))
side <- side[order(-side$pct_of_total_truncated_7L), ]

2.3 Negative components, and what they mean here

neg_all <- list()
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  cp       <- COMP[[sc]]
  neg      <- cp[cp$is_negative, ]
  item_var <- cp$var_signed[cp$effect == OBJECT]
  neg_all[[sc]] <- neg

  cat(sprintf("%-3s item variance %.6f (%.2f%%)   negatives %d of %d",
              sc, item_var, 100 * item_var / TOT_TR[[sc]], nrow(neg), nrow(cp)))
  if (nrow(neg)) {
    w <- neg[which.min(neg$var_signed), ]
    cat(sprintf("   most negative %s = %.3e (%.4f%% of item variance)",
                w$effect_short, w$var_signed, 100 * w$var_signed / item_var))
  }
  cat("\n")
}

#> 3L  item variance 0.424722 (68.48%)   negatives 8 of 31   most negative is = -8.806e-04 (-0.2073% of item variance)

neg_tbl <- do.call(rbind, neg_all)
if (nrow(neg_tbl)) {
  knitr::kable(neg_tbl[, c("scoring", "effect", "effect_short", "df", "var_signed")],
               digits = 8, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = "Components estimated below zero, both scorings.")
}

The diagnostic value is in the magnitude. A small negative is consistent with a near-zero component; a large negative warrants investigation.

Truncating the negatives to zero does not leave the coefficients unchanged. It raises the error terms by each truncated negative divided by its design denominator; τ is unaffected, because the item component itself is not negative. Balance has no bearing on that — what balance buys is that the method-of-moments estimates are exact, so the size of the shift can be reported rather than assumed. The next chunk prints it.

n_noobj <- DSIZE[setdiff(FACETS, OBJECT)]

mom_g <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(FALSE, TRUE), function(tr) {
    data.frame(dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc,
               components = ifelse(tr, "truncated", "signed"),
               t(g_coefficients(VC[[sc]], n_noobj, truncate = tr)),
               row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(mom_g, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Coefficients from signed vs truncated components, both scorings.")

mental_health_3L 3L truncated 0.424722 0.014661 0.015163 0.966632 0.965529 

# The quantity that settles the question: how much does truncation actually
# move the reported coefficients?
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  sg <- mom_g[mom_g$scoring == sc & mom_g$components == "signed", ]
  tr <- mom_g[mom_g$scoring == sc & mom_g$components == "truncated", ]
  vcs <- as.numeric(VC[[sc]])
  cat(sprintf("%-3s truncation shifts Erho2 by %.3e, Phi by %.3e;",
              sc, tr$Erho2 - sg$Erho2, tr$Phi - sg$Phi))
  cat(sprintf(" negative components sum %.3e (%.4f%% of total)\n",
              sum(pmin(vcs, 0)), 100 * abs(sum(pmin(vcs, 0))) / TOT_TR[[sc]]))
}

#> 3L  truncation shifts Erho2 by -7.437e-04, Phi by -1.187e-03; negative components sum -2.834e-03 (0.4570% of total)

3 Scale and sample sensitivities

The signed decomposition is repeated on rank-transformed scores and under every assignment of categories to ranks. These analyses assess nonlinear monotone rescoring and category-order sensitivity. Entropy-stratum estimates assess heterogeneity within the item sample; item-sampling uncertainty is handled by the bootstrap below.

# Categories in the seven-level severity order; the 7L score IS the category
# index, so the 7L array is the category array.
CATEGORIES <- names(MH7)
K   <- length(CATEGORIES)
a7  <- ARR[["7L"]]
DS7 <- DATASET_OF[["7L"]]
stopifnot(setequal(sort(unique(as.integer(a7))), seq_len(K)))

#' Item share and coefficients from a scored array, signed decomposition.
scale_erho <- function(a) {
  vc <- variance_components(a)
  g  <- g_coefficients(vc, n_noobj, truncate = TRUE)
  c(item_pct = 100 * vc[[OBJECT]] / sum(pmax(vc, 0)),
    Erho2 = g[["Erho2"]], Phi = g[["Phi"]])
}
perms_of <- function(v) if (length(v) <= 1) list(v) else
  do.call(c, lapply(seq_along(v), function(i)
    lapply(perms_of(v[-i]), function(p) c(v[i], p))))

# (1) rank transform: keeps the order and applies a nonlinear monotone rescoring
raw <- scale_erho(a7)
rnk <- scale_erho(array(rank(as.numeric(a7), ties.method = "average"), dim = dim(a7)))
scale_rank_transform <- data.frame(
  dataset = DS7, item_pct_raw = raw[["item_pct"]], item_pct_ranked = rnk[["item_pct"]],
  Erho2_raw = raw[["Erho2"]], Erho2_ranked = rnk[["Erho2"]],
  Phi_raw = raw[["Phi"]], Phi_ranked = rnk[["Phi"]],
  dErho2 = raw[["Erho2"]] - rnk[["Erho2"]], row.names = NULL)

# (2) every assignment of the seven categories to ranks 1..7 (5,040 orderings)
# A reversed scoring has identical variance components, so each reversal pair
# is one decomposition: keep the member with the lower first rank.
P   <- perms_of(seq_len(K))
P   <- P[vapply(P, function(p) p[1] < p[K], logical(1))]
res <- vapply(P, function(p) scale_erho(array(p[a7], dim = dim(a7))), numeric(3))
scale_permutation_distribution <- data.frame(
  dataset = DS7, n_orderings = length(P), n_orderings_with_reversals = 2L * length(P), Erho2_reported = raw[["Erho2"]],
  Erho2_min = min(res["Erho2", ]), Erho2_max = max(res["Erho2", ]),
  Erho2_median = median(res["Erho2", ]),
  Erho2_range = max(res["Erho2", ]) - min(res["Erho2", ]),
  Erho2_pctile_of_reported = 100 * mean(res["Erho2", ] <= raw[["Erho2"]]),
  item_pct_min = min(res["item_pct", ]), item_pct_max = max(res["item_pct", ]),
  row.names = NULL)

# (3) named orderings.  `alts` gives the category order, low to high; it is
# inverted to get category -> rank.
alts <- list(
  reported   = seq_len(K),
  reversed   = rev(seq_len(K)),
  # suicidal as the single most severe, the rest by typical clinical acuity
  acuity     = match(c("NORMAL", "STRESS", "ANXIETY", "PERSONALITY_DISORDER",
                       "DEPRESSION", "BIPOLAR", "SUICIDAL"), CATEGORIES),
  # internalising conditions first
  mood_first = match(c("NORMAL", "STRESS", "ANXIETY", "DEPRESSION", "SUICIDAL",
                       "BIPOLAR", "PERSONALITY_DISORDER"), CATEGORIES))
scale_named_orderings <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(alts), function(an) {
  p <- integer(K); p[alts[[an]]] <- seq_len(K)
  v <- scale_erho(array(p[a7], dim = dim(a7)))
  data.frame(dataset = DS7, ordering = an,
             categories_low_to_high = paste(CATEGORIES[alts[[an]]], collapse = " < "),
             item_pct = v[["item_pct"]], Erho2 = v[["Erho2"]], Phi = v[["Phi"]],
             row.names = NULL)
}))

# (4) constrained orderings: NORMAL fixed lowest and SUICIDAL fixed highest,
# the five arguable middle categories permuted (5! = 120).
MID <- 2:6
scale_constrained_ordering <- do.call(rbind, lapply(perms_of(MID), function(p) {
  sc <- integer(K); sc[1] <- 1L; sc[K] <- K; sc[p] <- 2:6
  v  <- scale_erho(array(sc[a7], dim = dim(a7)))
  data.frame(dataset = DS7, order = paste(CATEGORIES[order(sc)], collapse = " < "),
             is_reported = identical(sc, seq_len(K)),
             item_pct = v[["item_pct"]], Erho2 = v[["Erho2"]], Phi = v[["Phi"]],
             row.names = NULL)
}))

# Item entropy strata from the sampling frame (the mh_sample_100.csv the items
# were drawn with).  The array's item axis follows the factor levels of
# `item`, so strata are aligned by id, never by position.  Both scorings.
sam   <- read.csv(file.path(DATA_DIR, "mh_sample_100.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
strat <- setNames(as.character(sam$entropy_stratum), as.character(sam$item_id))[levels(DS[["7L"]]$item)]
if (anyNA(strat)) stop("entropy stratum missing for some items")
gcoeff_by_entropy_stratum <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(strat)), function(st) {
    keep <- which(strat == st)
    if (length(keep) < 5) return(NULL)
    v <- scale_erho(ARR[[sc]][keep, , , , , drop = FALSE])
    data.frame(dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, stratum = st, n_items = length(keep),
               item_pct = v[["item_pct"]], Erho2 = v[["Erho2"]], Phi = v[["Phi"]],
               row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))

4 Model definitions and sensitivity comparison

The reported specification begins from the instrument definition: each evaluator × prompt pair is an instrument configuration. Evaluator and prompt remain factorized because the 12 configurations are not independent: configurations that share an evaluator or a prompt also share structure. Configuration variation is therefore decomposed into evaluator, prompt, and evaluator × prompt terms; item × configuration variation is decomposed into item × evaluator, item × prompt, and their non-additive item:evaluator:prompt remainder. Temperature is a condition within a configuration, and seed is replication within configuration × temperature. The factorization represents known sharing among configurations; it does not make the purposively chosen evaluator and prompt levels independent, so generalization remains conditional on the observed pools.

Family 2 treats temperature as a configuration-specific protocol condition and seed as replication within configuration × temperature. That nesting is a modelling assumption, not a consequence of the factorial crossing. Its three members differ only on the item side: additive, complete, and complete with temperature-specific item drift. ML-BIC selects the reported member within Family 2; params$report_spec records that selection and is checked against the fitted comparison. The other complete member is always carried as its contrast. The remaining specifications evaluate alternative instrument definitions.

#' All subsets of the five facets up to order k, as a random-effects formula.
terms_upto <- function(k) unlist(lapply(seq_len(k), function(r)
  combn(FACETS, r, FUN = function(x) paste(x, collapse = ":"), simplify = TRUE)))

form_from_terms <- function(tm) as.formula(
  paste("score ~ 1 +", paste(sprintf("(1|%s)", tm), collapse = " + ")))

# The reported specification supplies the reported D-study and intervals.
REPORT_SPEC <- params$report_spec
# The other Family 2 member with the complete item structure: the pooled-
# temperature specification when drift is reported, the drift specification
# when the pooled one is.  It is always projected beside the reported one.
PAIR_SPEC  <- if (identical(REPORT_SPEC, "f2_complete_drift")) "f2_complete" else "f2_complete_drift"
PAIR_LABEL <- if (identical(REPORT_SPEC, "f2_complete_drift")) "pooled-temperature sensitivity" else "drift sensitivity"

# Models are grouped by scientific role, not by BIC order. REPORT_SPEC determines
# which Family 2 member is reported; list position has no selection meaning.
FORMS <- list(
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # FAMILY 1E -- single-facet instrument: the EVALUATOR.  Everything outside
  # the instrument is a replication
  # nested within it, in the order prompt, temperature, seed: prompt effects
  # are not shared across evaluators (no prompt main effect and no item x
  # prompt term), temperature nests within the evaluator-prompt cell, and seed
  # within temperature.  The three members mirror the three Family 2 members
  # minus the shared prompt effects, so the 1E / Family 2 contrast
  # isolates one question: whether prompt effects are shared across
  # evaluators or evaluator-specific.  That is a covariance assumption; which
  # facets constitute the instrument remains the measurement-design choice.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  # FAMILY 1E, complete: item x evaluator is the only item-by-instrument term
  # (with a single instrument facet, additive and complete coincide).
  f1e_complete = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | item:evaluator) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # FAMILY 1E, complete with prompt interaction: adds item x prompt-within-
  # evaluator.  Counterpart of f2_complete without the shared prompt effects.
  f1e_complete_prompt = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | item:evaluator) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | item:evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # FAMILY 1E, complete with temperature interaction: adds item x temperature-
  # within-cell.  Counterpart of f2_complete_drift without the shared prompt
  # effects.
  f1e_complete_drift = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | item:evaluator) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | item:evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | item:evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # FAMILY 1P -- single-facet instrument: the PROMPT, the mirror of 1E.  The
  # evaluator is a replication nested within it (evaluator within prompt,
  # temperature within the cell, seed within temperature): no evaluator main
  # effect and no item x evaluator term, so no evaluator effect is shared
  # across prompts.  The three members are the Family 2 members minus the
  # shared evaluator effects, the exact mirror of Family 1E, so the two
  # single-facet families show which facet can stand as the instrument.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # FAMILY 1P, complete: item x prompt is the only item-by-instrument term.
  f1p_complete = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | prompt) + (1 | item:prompt) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),
  # FAMILY 1P, complete with evaluator interaction: adds item x evaluator-
  # within-prompt.  Counterpart of f2_complete without the shared evaluator effects.
  f1p_complete_eval = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | prompt) + (1 | item:prompt) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | item:evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),
  # FAMILY 1P, complete with temperature interaction: adds item x temperature-
  # within-cell.  Counterpart of f2_complete_drift without the shared evaluator
  # effects.
  f1p_complete_drift = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | prompt) + (1 | item:prompt) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | item:evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | item:evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # FAMILY 2, COMPLETE (temperature pooled): factorized evaluator-prompt
  # instrument configuration. The i:e,
  # i:p, and i:e:p terms jointly represent item x configuration variation;
  # i:e:p is its non-additive remainder. Temperature and seed remain nested
  # protocol/replication conditions within the configuration.
  f2_complete = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | prompt) +
    (1 | item:evaluator) + (1 | item:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | item:evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # FAMILY 2, COMPLETE WITH DRIFT: adds item x configuration x temperature to
  # test whether item ordering changes across temperatures within a fixed
  # evaluator-prompt configuration.
  f2_complete_drift = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | prompt) +
    (1 | item:evaluator) + (1 | item:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | item:evaluator:prompt) + (1 | item:evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # NON-ADDITIVE CONFIGURATION ABLATION: removes only i:e:p. The additive i:e
  # and i:p components remain, while their configuration-specific remainder is
  # pooled.
  f2_additive = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | prompt) +
    (1 | item:evaluator) + (1 | item:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:prompt) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) + (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # TEMPERATURE-INCLUSIVE INSTRUMENT.  The two models below promote
  # temperature to a component of the instrument, so the instrument is the
  # (evaluator, prompt, temperature) triple and SEED is the only
  # within-instrument replication.
  #
  # This is not the same as adding item:evaluator:prompt:temp to the primary.
  # There, temperature is still a nesting condition and e:p:t absorbs the
  # temperature main effect along with e:t and p:t.  Promoting temperature
  # means those terms are estimated in their own right, on both the
  # instrument side and the item side -- which is what "temperature is part
  # of the instrument" actually asserts.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  # TEMPERATURE-INCLUSIVE, ADDITIVE ITEM TERMS.  Instrument side carries every
  # subset of {evaluator, prompt, temperature}; item side carries only the
  # additive components.
  f3_additive = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | prompt) + (1 | temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:temp) + (1 | prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | item:evaluator) + (1 | item:prompt) + (1 | item:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # TEMPERATURE-INCLUSIVE, FULL ITEM-BY-INSTRUMENT STRUCTURE.  Adds every
  # non-additive item-by-instrument term, ending at item x evaluator x prompt
  # x temperature; item x instrument x seed is the residual, since one
  # observation per cell confounds it with error.
  f3_complete = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | prompt) + (1 | temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:temp) + (1 | prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | item:evaluator) + (1 | item:prompt) + (1 | item:temp) +
    (1 | item:evaluator:prompt) + (1 | item:evaluator:temp) +
    (1 | item:prompt:temp) + (1 | item:evaluator:prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # LEGACY NESTING SENSITIVITY: seed is nested within e:p:t, while temperature
  # remains a crossed facet with its main effect and two-way interactions.
  nested_seed = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | prompt) + (1 | temp) +
    (1 | item:evaluator) + (1 | item:prompt) + (1 | item:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:temp) + (1 | prompt:temp) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt:temp:seed),

  # SYMMETRIC TWO-WAY BENCHMARK: all facet main effects and pairwise
  # interactions, with no design-specific higher-order term.
  full_crossed = score ~ 1 +
    (1 | item) + (1 | evaluator) + (1 | prompt) + (1 | temp) + (1 | seed) +
    (1 | item:evaluator) + (1 | item:prompt) + (1 | item:temp) + (1 | item:seed) +
    (1 | evaluator:prompt) + (1 | evaluator:temp) + (1 | evaluator:seed) +
    (1 | prompt:temp) + (1 | prompt:seed) + (1 | temp:seed)
)

SPEC_ROLE <- c(
  # ---- main family: the instrument configuration is the evaluator-prompt pair ----
  f2_complete       = "Family 2, complete: item-by-configuration terms, temperature pooled",
  f2_complete_drift = "Family 2, complete with temperature interaction: adds item x configuration x temperature",
  f2_additive       = "Family 2, additive: omit the non-additive item-by-configuration remainder",
  # ---- structural sensitivities: a different instrument configuration ----
  f1e_complete        = "Family 1E, complete: unit = evaluator; prompt, temperature and seed replicate within it",
  f1e_complete_prompt = "Family 1E, complete with prompt interaction: adds item x prompt within evaluator",
  f1e_complete_drift  = "Family 1E, complete with prompt and temperature interactions: adds item x temperature within cell",
  f1p_complete       = "Family 1P, complete: unit = prompt; evaluator, temperature and seed replicate within it",
  f1p_complete_eval  = "Family 1P, complete with evaluator interaction: adds item x evaluator within prompt",
  f1p_complete_drift = "Family 1P, complete with evaluator and temperature interactions: adds item x temperature within cell",
  f3_additive       = "Family 3, additive: unit = evaluator x prompt x temperature",
  f3_complete       = "Family 3, complete: unit = evaluator x prompt x temperature",
  # ---- outside the family structure ----
  nested_seed       = "Benchmark: legacy seed nesting, no coherent configuration",
  full_crossed      = "Benchmark: symmetric main effects and all two-way interactions"
)

# Which models constitute the main comparison.  The others are reported but kept
# out of the headline table: a benchmark or an underfit control answers a
# different question from "which definition of the instrument configuration fits", and
# mixing them into one BIC ranking makes the ranking harder to read, not more
# complete.
# Family 2 is the primary instrument model. Its three members form the selection
# set; Families 1 and 3 are cross-family structural sensitivities.

# Presentation order, applied once here so every table that iterates over the
# specifications inherits it: Families 1E and 1P, then 2, then 3, each family's members in
# order of increasing item structure (the temperature-interaction members beside
# the specifications they extend), and the two benchmarks last.  The list above is grouped by how the formulas
# were built, which is not the order Table 1 presents them in.
SPEC_ORDER <- c("f1e_complete", "f1e_complete_prompt", "f1e_complete_drift",
                  "f1p_complete", "f1p_complete_eval", "f1p_complete_drift",
                  "f2_additive", "f2_complete", "f2_complete_drift",
                  "f3_additive", "f3_complete",
                  "nested_seed", "full_crossed")
stopifnot(setequal(SPEC_ORDER, names(FORMS)))
# The Family 1 ladder, and its relation to Family 2, asserted rather than assumed.
stopifnot(
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1e_complete_prompt), "term.labels"),
           c(attr(terms(FORMS$f1e_complete), "term.labels"), "1 | item:evaluator:prompt")),
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1e_complete_drift), "term.labels"),
           c(attr(terms(FORMS$f1e_complete_prompt), "term.labels"), "1 | item:evaluator:prompt:temp")),
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1e_complete_prompt), "term.labels"),
           setdiff(attr(terms(FORMS$f2_complete), "term.labels"), c("1 | prompt", "1 | item:prompt"))),
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1e_complete_drift), "term.labels"),
           setdiff(attr(terms(FORMS$f2_complete_drift), "term.labels"), c("1 | prompt", "1 | item:prompt"))),
  # Family 1P: the mirror, Family 2 minus the shared evaluator effects.
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1p_complete_eval), "term.labels"),
           c(attr(terms(FORMS$f1p_complete), "term.labels"), "1 | item:evaluator:prompt")),
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1p_complete_drift), "term.labels"),
           c(attr(terms(FORMS$f1p_complete_eval), "term.labels"), "1 | item:evaluator:prompt:temp")),
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1p_complete_eval), "term.labels"),
           setdiff(attr(terms(FORMS$f2_complete), "term.labels"), c("1 | evaluator", "1 | item:evaluator"))),
  setequal(attr(terms(FORMS$f1p_complete_drift), "term.labels"),
           setdiff(attr(terms(FORMS$f2_complete_drift), "term.labels"), c("1 | evaluator", "1 | item:evaluator"))))

# The grid digest elsewhere in this document covers the D-study contract.  It does not cover the
# specifications themselves, which is where a silent divergence between the five
# documents would actually do damage: an edited formula in one file changes the
# model without changing any assertion.  This digests the nine specifications by
# their sorted term labels.
.spec_contract <- paste(paste0(sort(names(FORMS), method = "radix"), "=",
  vapply(sort(names(FORMS), method = "radix"), function(m)
    paste(sort(attr(terms(FORMS[[m]]), "term.labels"), method = "radix"), collapse = ","),
    character(1))), collapse = "|")
SPEC_MD5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(local({
  f <- tempfile(); writeLines(.spec_contract, f, sep = ""); f
})))
stopifnot(identical(SPEC_MD5, "f2c9725bf5d8cfa9344a07aae3f8a606"))

FORMS      <- FORMS[SPEC_ORDER]
SPEC_ROLE <- SPEC_ROLE[SPEC_ORDER]

# Term labels of every specification, captured before any subset is taken, so
# the residual-composition classification can name the terms of a
# specification whether or not this stage fits it.
TERMS_OF <- lapply(FORMS, function(f) sub("^1 \\| ", "", attr(terms(f), "term.labels")))

REPORTED_FAMILY <- c("f2_additive", "f2_complete", "f2_complete_drift")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# What gets fitted, and what gets bootstrapped, are two separate questions.
#
# Family 2 defines the primary instrument model, and its three members are
# compared by ML-BIC. Families 1 and 3 are retained as cross-family structural
# sensitivities. The full-grid D-study and bootstrap intervals use the selected
# Family 2 member. The two legacy benchmarks are fitted only when
# params$benchmarks is TRUE, and hierarchy controls only when params$hierarchy
# is TRUE.
#
# The bootstrap is a separate stage (params$stage).  It is by far the most
# expensive step, and there is no reason to spend it before the reported
# specification is settled: stage "models" fits and compares, stage "bootstrap"
# does the same and then attaches intervals to the reported specification.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
FAMILY_SPECS <- c("f1e_complete", "f1e_complete_prompt", "f1e_complete_drift",
                  "f1p_complete", "f1p_complete_eval", "f1p_complete_drift",
                  "f2_additive", "f2_complete", "f2_complete_drift",
                  "f3_additive", "f3_complete")
# Cross-family BIC is retained as a sensitivity; it does not redefine the
# primary Family 2 instrument.
BIC_UNIVERSE <- FAMILY_SPECS   # every family member, the Family 2 temperature-interaction member included
if (!params$stage %in% c("models", "bootstrap"))
  stop('stage must be "models" or "bootstrap"')
if (!isTRUE(params$benchmarks)) {
  # Both complete Family 2 members are always fitted, whichever is reported: the
  # contrast between them measures what pooling item x evaluator x prompt x
  # temperature into the residual does to the projections (that pooled variation
  # is divided by n_s under projection, yet extra seeds cannot average away
  # item-specific temperature drift).
  FORMS      <- FORMS[intersect(names(FORMS), c(FAMILY_SPECS, "f2_complete_drift"))]
  SPEC_ROLE <- SPEC_ROLE[names(FORMS)]
}
# The reported specification must be among what is fitted, whatever the subset.
if (!REPORT_SPEC %in% names(FORMS))
  stop("report_spec '", REPORT_SPEC, "' is not among the fitted specifications")


# What each family treats as one instrument configuration.  These counts are
# descriptive labels for the families, NOT D-study divisors: gcoef() divides
# each variance component by the levels of the non-item facets that component
# actually contains, so the family changes which components exist and how each
# is scaled rather than supplying one divisor of its own.  The configurations
# are also not mutually independent -- two that share an evaluator or a prompt
# remain dependent, which is exactly why evaluator, prompt and their
# interaction are estimated separately rather than as one atomic factor.
SPEC_FAMILY <- c(
  f2_complete = "2", f2_complete_drift = "2", f2_additive = "2",
  f1e_complete = "1E", f1e_complete_prompt = "1E", f1e_complete_drift = "1E",
  f1p_complete = "1P", f1p_complete_eval = "1P", f1p_complete_drift = "1P",
  f3_additive = "3", f3_complete = "3",
  nested_seed = NA_character_, full_crossed = NA_character_,
  # Deliberate, not an oversight: the hierarchy controls belong to no family.
  order1 = NA_character_, order2 = NA_character_,
  order3 = NA_character_, order4 = NA_character_
)
FAMILY_CONFIG <- c("1E" = "evaluator", "1P" = "prompt", "2" = "evaluator x prompt",
                 "3" = "evaluator x prompt x temperature")
FAMILY_N_CONFIG <- c("1E" = 4L, "1P" = 3L, "2" = 12L, "3" = 72L)

# The order-truncated family.  order2 is the same model as full_crossed, so it
# is not fitted twice.
#
# max_order defaults to 3. Order 1 is an underfit control; order 3 is a
# hierarchy-complete check containing every three-way interaction; order 4 is
# the saturated sensitivity and is fitted only when explicitly requested.
if (!params$max_order %in% 1:4) stop("max_order must be one of 1, 2, 3, or 4")
for (k in if (isTRUE(params$hierarchy)) seq_len(params$max_order) else integer(0)) {
  if (k == 2) next
  mn <- sprintf("order%d", k)
  FORMS[[mn]] <- form_from_terms(terms_upto(k))
  SPEC_ROLE[[mn]] <- switch(as.character(k),
    "1" = "Notebook-only hierarchy control: main effects only (not reported in the manuscript)",
    "3" = "Notebook-only hierarchy check: all interactions through order three (not reported in the manuscript)",
    "4" = "Notebook-only saturated check: interactions through order four (not reported in the manuscript)")
}

# The bootstrap stage fits the same comparison set and then resamples the
# reported specification, so one render in that stage is the complete document.

stopifnot(all(names(FORMS) %in% names(SPEC_ROLE)))

# maxfun matches the value stated in the manuscript Methods (100000).
CTRL <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000))

data.frame(
  spec  = names(FORMS),
  role = unname(SPEC_ROLE[names(FORMS)]),
  family = unname(SPEC_FAMILY[names(FORMS)]),
  n_terms = vapply(FORMS, function(f) length(attr(terms(f), "term.labels")),
                   integer(1)),
  row.names = NULL) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Specifications to be fitted, by instrument-configuration family.")

4.1 What each specification absorbs

This heuristic classification treats every full-crossed effect as either estimated by name, pooled into one of its nesting terms, or left in its residual. One rule classifies all 31 effects under any specification: an effect that matches a term exactly is explicit; an effect contained in an explicit term with the same item membership is pooled into the smallest such term; anything else is residual. The classification is reported for the reported specification and, for comparison, for the other Family 2 members: the complete specification without temperature drift, and the reduced one without the non-additive item-by-configuration term, which is the specification the submitted analysis reported. The second classification is what shows which item interactions that reduction pooled into its residual.

#' Where a full-crossed effect lands in a specification, given that
#' specification's random-effect term labels.  An effect matching a term
#' exactly is explicit; an effect contained in an explicit term with the same
#' item membership is pooled into the smallest such term; anything else is
#' residual.
home_in_spec <- function(parts, term_labels) {
  has_i <- OBJECT %in% parts
  tsets <- strsplit(term_labels, ":", fixed = TRUE)
  same  <- vapply(tsets, function(t) (OBJECT %in% t) == has_i, logical(1))
  exact <- vapply(tsets, function(t) setequal(t, parts), logical(1))
  if (any(exact)) return(c(home = term_labels[which(exact)[1]], kind = "explicit"))
  sup <- which(same & vapply(tsets, function(t) all(parts %in% t), logical(1)))
  if (length(sup)) {
    sup <- sup[order(lengths(tsets[sup]))][1]
    return(c(home = term_labels[sup], kind = "pooled"))
  }
  c(home = "Residual", kind = "residual")
}

HOME_SPECS <- c(reported = REPORT_SPEC, complete = "f2_complete", reduced = "f2_additive")
HOME_SPECS <- HOME_SPECS[!duplicated(HOME_SPECS)]
res_rows <- list()
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  cp <- COMP[[sc]]
  parts_c <- strsplit(cp$effect, ":", fixed = TRUE)
  for (hs in names(HOME_SPECS)) {
    h <- t(vapply(parts_c, home_in_spec, character(2),
                  term_labels = TERMS_OF[[HOME_SPECS[[hs]]]]))
    cp[[paste0("home_", hs)]]      <- unname(h[, "home"])
    cp[[paste0("home_kind_", hs)]] <- unname(h[, "kind"])
  }
  COMP[[sc]] <- cp
  for (hs in names(HOME_SPECS)) {
    hcol <- cp[[paste0("home_", hs)]]
    for (h in unique(hcol)) {
      g <- cp[hcol == h, ]
      res_rows[[length(res_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc,
        specification = unname(HOME_SPECS[[hs]]), role = hs,
        home = h, kind = if (h == "Residual") "residual" else "term", n_components = nrow(g),
        sum_var_signed = sum(g$var_signed),
        sum_var_truncated = sum(g$var_truncated),
        pct_of_total = 100 * sum(g$var_truncated) / TOT_TR[[sc]],
        largest_component = g$effect_short[which.max(g$var_truncated)],
        largest_pct = max(g$pct_of_total_truncated), row.names = NULL)
    }
  }
}
comp <- do.call(rbind, COMP)
resid_comp <- do.call(rbind, res_rows)

Candidate specifications are fitted under ML (params$comparison_estimator) for the BIC diagnostic; the reported specification, f2_complete_drift, is then refitted under REML (params$report_estimator) for the fitted-model results reported here: variance components, coefficients, D-study projections and their bootstrap intervals. The scoring-order and entropy-stratum sensitivities are truncated method-of-moments calculations on the saturated array and refit nothing.

Under REML, a restricted likelihood is the likelihood of a set of error contrasts determined by the fixed-effects design matrix alone, so two restricted likelihoods are comparable only when that matrix is the same. Every specification here is score ~ 1: the fixed-effect structure is one intercept throughout, so the restricted likelihoods evaluate the same function under different covariance structures and the information criteria are admissible; they then count covariance parameters only, with the penalty over \(n - p\). Under ML the intercept is counted as well and the penalty is over \(n\). ML supplies the model-selection likelihood. REML supplies the reported variance-component estimates because the estimands are variance components, and ML’s downward bias in them scales with the ratio of parameters to the relevant degrees of freedom: comfortable for the item component (100 items), poor for the instrumentation components — evaluator carries 3 degrees of freedom, prompt 2, their interaction 6 — and those are exactly the components \(\Phi\) depends on.

BIC is reported as a relative-fit diagnostic, using converged fits only; singularity is flagged at a tolerance of 1e-5 on the relative Cholesky factor, tighter than lme4’s default of 1e-4. f2_complete_drift is refitted under REML for the variance components, coefficients, Wald intervals, D-study projections, and item-cluster bootstrap refits. The full expected-mean-squares decomposition remains a separate model-structure diagnostic rather than a second bootstrap estimand.

Only variance-component vectors are retained from the sensitivity fits. The reported specification is refitted below because its Hessian is needed. Warnings remain visible, and convergence codes, messages, singularity, and runtime are recorded for every specification.

# A previous render of this document writes the comparison table and the REML
# component vector of every specification.  When nothing upstream has changed,
# those are reloaded and the two fitting loops are skipped; the guard below
# refuses a saved comparison whose specification set, term counts or estimators
# differ from this render's.
REUSE_DIR <- if (nzchar(params$reuse_from)) normalizePath(params$reuse_from, mustWork = TRUE) else OUT_DIR
reuse_mc <- file.path(REUSE_DIR, sprintf("uni_model_comparison_%s.csv", DATASET_OF[SCORINGS]))
reuse_cb <- file.path(REUSE_DIR, sprintf("uni_components_by_spec_%s.csv", DATASET_OF[SCORINGS]))
REUSED   <- isTRUE(params$reuse_comparison) && all(file.exists(c(reuse_mc, reuse_cb)))
CB_STATUS <- "fitted"   # overwritten with the companion file's own status when the comparison is reused
if (!REUSED) {
cmp_rows <- list(); V_BY_SPEC_ML <- list()

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
V_BY_SPEC_ML[[sc]] <- list()
for (mn in names(FORMS)) {
  t0  <- Sys.time()
  fit <- try(lmer(FORMS[[mn]], data = DS[[sc]], REML = USE_REML_COMPARE, control = CTRL),
             silent = TRUE)
  secs <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))

  if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] %-24s FAILED (%.0fs): %s\n", sc, mn, secs,
                sub("\n.*", "", as.character(fit))))
    cmp_rows[[length(cmp_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, spec = mn,
      comparison_estimator = COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR, n_re_terms = NA_integer_,
      logLik = NA_real_, AIC = NA_real_, BIC = NA_real_,
      singular = NA, converged = FALSE,
      conv_code = NA_integer_, conv_message = "fit failed",
      secs = secs, row.names = NULL)
    next
  }

  # Computed once and used by both the table and the console line.
  n_cov   <- length(getME(fit, "theta")) + 1L
  # Under REML the intercept is integrated out and the penalty is over n - p;
  # under ML it is a free parameter of the likelihood and the penalty is over n.
  k_ic    <- if (USE_REML_COMPARE) n_cov else n_cov + P_FIX
  n_ic    <- if (USE_REML_COMPARE) nobs(fit) - P_FIX else nobs(fit)
  aic_val <- -2 * as.numeric(logLik(fit)) + 2 * k_ic
  bic_val <- -2 * as.numeric(logLik(fit)) + k_ic * log(n_ic)
  vd <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
  V_BY_SPEC_ML[[sc]][[mn]] <- setNames(vd$vcov, vd$grp)

  # lme4 signals convergence trouble through optinfo, not through conditions,
  # so convergence is read off the fit rather than inferred from "no error".
  #
  # The singularity message lives in the same slot as genuine convergence
  # warnings, but a singular fit HAS converged -- its optimum simply sits on
  # the boundary, which is expected here and already has its own column.
  # Treating it as non-convergence would disqualify nearly every candidate.
  conv_code <- fit@optinfo$conv$opt
  msgs      <- unlist(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages)
  msgs      <- msgs[!grepl("singular", msgs, fixed = TRUE)]
  conv_msg  <- paste(msgs, collapse = "; ")

  cmp_rows[[length(cmp_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, spec = mn,
    comparison_estimator = COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR, n_re_terms = length(getME(fit, "flist")),
    logLik = as.numeric(logLik(fit)),
    # One BIC convention across all five documents.  lme4's BIC() counts the
    # fixed intercept and uses log(n) even for a REML fit; under REML the fixed
    # effects are integrated out of the objective, so the criterion counts
    # covariance parameters only and the penalty uses n - p.  The two differ by
    # p = 1 parameter for every specification here, so the offset is constant to
    # any precision anyone prints: the varying part is
    # (n_theta + 1) * log(n / (n - p)), about 4e-4 BIC units against values of
    # order 1e4.
    AIC = aic_val,
    BIC = bic_val,
    singular = isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-5),
    converged = (conv_code == 0L && !nzchar(conv_msg)),
    conv_code = conv_code, conv_message = conv_msg,
    secs = secs, row.names = NULL)
  cat(sprintf("[%s] %-24s BIC = %12.2f  singular = %-5s conv = %-5s (%.0fs)%s\n",
              sc, mn, bic_val,
              isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-5),
              (conv_code == 0L && !nzchar(conv_msg)), secs,
              if (nzchar(conv_msg)) paste0("  [", conv_msg, "]") else ""))
  rm(fit); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}
}

model_comparison <- bind_rows(cmp_rows)
model_comparison$data_md5 <- DATA_MD5
model_comparison$spec_md5 <- SPEC_MD5
model_comparison$seed     <- params$seed
model_comparison$maxfun   <- CTRL$optCtrl$maxfun
REUSE_NOTE <- "comparison fitted in this render"
model_comparison$role   <- unname(SPEC_ROLE[model_comparison$spec])
model_comparison$family <- unname(SPEC_FAMILY[model_comparison$spec])
model_comparison$in_reported_family <- model_comparison$spec %in% REPORTED_FAMILY
model_comparison$in_family_comparison <- model_comparison$spec %in% FAMILY_SPECS
model_comparison$is_reported <- model_comparison$spec == REPORT_SPEC
model_comparison$is_bic_best <- FALSE
model_comparison$is_bic_best_any <- FALSE

# BIC is calculated separately because the numerical outcome changes when seven
# levels are collapsed to three.
BIC_BEST <- list()
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  m  <- model_comparison[model_comparison$scoring == sc, ]
  el <- m[m$converged %in% TRUE & m$spec %in% BIC_UNIVERSE, ]
  if (!nrow(el)) stop("no cross-family BIC sensitivity specification converged for scoring ", sc)
  BIC_BEST[[sc]] <- el$spec[which.min(el$BIC)]
  model_comparison$is_bic_best[
    model_comparison$scoring == sc &
      model_comparison$spec == BIC_BEST[[sc]]] <- TRUE

  pr <- m[m$spec == REPORT_SPEC, ]
  if (nrow(pr) != 1L || !isTRUE(pr$converged))
    stop(REPORT_SPEC, " did not converge for scoring ", sc)

  f2 <- m[m$converged %in% TRUE & m$spec %in% REPORTED_FAMILY, ]
  if (!nrow(f2)) stop("no Family 2 specification converged for scoring ", sc)
  family2_best_fit <- f2$spec[which.min(f2$BIC)]
  if (!identical(REPORT_SPEC, family2_best_fit))
    stop("report_spec must equal the within-Family 2 ML-BIC winner for ", sc,
         ": ", family2_best_fit, "; current report_spec is ", REPORT_SPEC)

  bic_best_any <- m$spec[which.min(m$BIC)]
  model_comparison$is_bic_best_any[
    model_comparison$scoring == sc &
      model_comparison$spec == bic_best_any] <- TRUE
  if (!identical(bic_best_any, BIC_BEST[[sc]])) {
    cat(sprintf("NOTE [%s]: overall BIC minimum is %s; cross-family converged minimum is %s.\n",
                sc, bic_best_any, BIC_BEST[[sc]]))
    print(m[m$spec == bic_best_any,
            c("spec", "BIC", "singular", "conv_code", "conv_message")],
          row.names = FALSE)
  }
}

# Reliability and D-study sensitivity use REML for every specification.
V_BY_SPEC_REML <- setNames(lapply(SCORINGS, function(x) list()), SCORINGS)
reml_rows <- list()
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  ml_ok <- model_comparison$spec[
    model_comparison$scoring == sc & model_comparison$converged %in% TRUE]
  for (mn in ml_ok) {
    fit <- try(lmer(FORMS[[mn]], data = DS[[sc]], REML = TRUE, control = CTRL),
               silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) {
      reml_rows[[length(reml_rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        scoring = sc, spec = mn, reml_converged = FALSE,
        reml_singular = NA, reml_message = "fit failed", row.names = NULL)
      next
    }
    conv_code <- fit@optinfo$conv$opt
    msgs <- unlist(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages)
    msgs <- msgs[!grepl("singular", msgs, fixed = TRUE)]
    conv_msg <- paste(msgs, collapse = "; ")
    ok <- conv_code == 0L && !nzchar(conv_msg)
    if (ok) {
      vd <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
      V_BY_SPEC_REML[[sc]][[mn]] <- setNames(vd$vcov, vd$grp)
    }
    reml_rows[[length(reml_rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
      scoring = sc, spec = mn, reml_converged = ok,
      reml_singular = isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-5),
      reml_message = conv_msg, row.names = NULL)
    rm(fit); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
  }
}
model_comparison <- left_join(model_comparison, bind_rows(reml_rows),
                              by = c("scoring", "spec"))
V_BY_SPEC <- V_BY_SPEC_REML
} else {
  model_comparison <- do.call(rbind, lapply(reuse_mc, read.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  cb <- do.call(rbind, lapply(reuse_cb, read.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  fp_cols <- c("data_md5", "spec_md5", "seed", "maxfun")
  # The component table is a separate file and must carry the same run
  # fingerprint as the summary; otherwise an interrupted export could pair a
  # current summary with stale components while the summary alone "verifies".
  # Returns the file's own verification status, which travels separately from
  # the summary's: an unstamped companion accepted under reuse_from is never
  # described as verified and is re-exported without a fingerprint.
  check_companion <- function(x, what) {
    if (all(fp_cols %in% names(x))) {
      if (!all(x$data_md5 == DATA_MD5) || !all(x$spec_md5 == SPEC_MD5) ||
          !all(x$seed == params$seed) || !all(x$maxfun == CTRL$optCtrl$maxfun))
        stop("saved ", what, " was written by another run (data, specifications, seed or optimizer ",
             "settings differ); rerender with reuse_comparison = FALSE")
      "verified"
    } else if (!nzchar(params$reuse_from))
      stop("saved ", what, " has no fingerprint; pass reuse_from explicitly to accept it, ",
           "or rerender with reuse_comparison = FALSE")
    else "unstamped"
  }
  companion_phrase <- function(status, what)
    if (identical(status, "verified")) paste(what, "fingerprint verified") else paste(what, "accepted without a fingerprint (reuse_from given explicitly)")
  CB_STATUS <- check_companion(cb, "component table")
  cb <- cb[setdiff(names(cb), fp_cols)]
  companion_note <- companion_phrase(CB_STATUS, "component table")
  if (all(fp_cols %in% names(model_comparison))) {
    if (!all(model_comparison$data_md5 == DATA_MD5) || !all(model_comparison$spec_md5 == SPEC_MD5) ||
        !all(model_comparison$seed == params$seed) || !all(model_comparison$maxfun == CTRL$optCtrl$maxfun))
      stop("saved comparison was fitted on other data, specifications, seed or optimizer settings; ",
           "rerender with reuse_comparison = FALSE")
    REUSE_NOTE <- paste0("summary fingerprint verified (data, specifications, seed, maxfun); ", companion_note)
  } else if (nzchar(params$reuse_from)) {
    REUSE_NOTE <- paste0("saved comparison predates the fingerprint columns; accepted because reuse_from was given explicitly; ", companion_note)
  } else stop("saved comparison has no fingerprint; pass reuse_from explicitly to accept it, ",
              "or rerender with reuse_comparison = FALSE")
  need <- vapply(FORMS, function(f) length(attr(terms(f), "term.labels")), integer(1))
  for (sc in SCORINGS) {
    m <- model_comparison[model_comparison$scoring == sc, ]
    have <- m$n_re_terms[match(names(FORMS), m$spec)]
    if (anyNA(have) || !identical(as.integer(have), unname(need)))
      stop("saved comparison for scoring ", sc, " does not match this render's specification set; ",
           "rerender with reuse_comparison = FALSE")
  }
  if (!all(model_comparison$comparison_estimator == COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR) ||
      !all(cb$components_estimator == REPORT_ESTIMATOR))
    stop("saved comparison used other estimators; rerender with reuse_comparison = FALSE")
  model_comparison <- model_comparison[model_comparison$spec %in% names(FORMS), ]
  # Empty message columns come back from the CSV as NA; restore the empty string.
  for (cc in intersect(c("conv_message", "reml_message"), names(model_comparison)))
    model_comparison[[cc]][is.na(model_comparison[[cc]])] <- ""
  # Labels and family tags come from this render's constants, not the saved file.
  model_comparison$role   <- unname(SPEC_ROLE[model_comparison$spec])
  model_comparison$family <- unname(SPEC_FAMILY[model_comparison$spec])
  model_comparison$in_reported_family   <- model_comparison$spec %in% REPORTED_FAMILY
  model_comparison$in_family_comparison <- model_comparison$spec %in% FAMILY_SPECS
  model_comparison$is_reported <- model_comparison$spec == REPORT_SPEC
  V_BY_SPEC <- lapply(setNames(SCORINGS, SCORINGS), function(sc) {
    x <- cb[cb$scoring == sc & cb$spec %in% names(FORMS), ]
    lapply(split(x, x$spec), function(y) setNames(y$variance, y$source))
  })
  BIC_BEST <- lapply(setNames(SCORINGS, SCORINGS), function(sc) {
    m <- model_comparison[model_comparison$scoring == sc &
                          model_comparison$converged %in% TRUE &
                          model_comparison$spec %in% BIC_UNIVERSE, ]
    m$spec[which.min(m$BIC)]
  })
  cat(sprintf("comparison fits reused from %s (written %s): %d rows, both scorings\n",
              sub(".*01_R1_WORKING/", "01_R1_WORKING/", REUSE_DIR), format(file.mtime(reuse_mc[1])), nrow(model_comparison)))
}

FAMILY2_BEST <- setNames(vector("list", length(SCORINGS)), SCORINGS)
model_comparison$is_family2_best <- FALSE
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  m <- model_comparison[
    model_comparison$scoring == sc &
      model_comparison$converged %in% TRUE &
      model_comparison$spec %in% REPORTED_FAMILY, ]
  if (!nrow(m)) stop("no Family 2 specification converged for scoring ", sc)
  FAMILY2_BEST[[sc]] <- m$spec[which.min(m$BIC)]
  model_comparison$is_family2_best[
    model_comparison$scoring == sc &
      model_comparison$spec == FAMILY2_BEST[[sc]]] <- TRUE
  if (!identical(REPORT_SPEC, FAMILY2_BEST[[sc]]))
    stop("report_spec must equal the within-Family 2 ML-BIC winner for ", sc,
         ": ", FAMILY2_BEST[[sc]], "; current report_spec is ", REPORT_SPEC)
}
for (sc in SCORINGS) if (!REPORT_SPEC %in% names(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]]))
  stop(REPORT_SPEC, " REML refit failed for scoring ", sc)
# Roles are assigned at run time from the parameters, never stored in labels.
model_comparison$report_role <- ifelse(model_comparison$spec == REPORT_SPEC, "reported",
                                ifelse(model_comparison$spec == PAIR_SPEC, PAIR_LABEL, ""))

                                    model_comparison$BIC), ],
             row.names = FALSE, digits = 4,
             caption = sprintf("The fitted specifications under %s, ordered by BIC.", COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR))

4.2 The non-additive item-by-configuration term, as one number

# The BIC cost of omitting item x evaluator x prompt from the reported
# specification, everything else held, per scoring.  Available whenever both
# Family 2 specifications were fitted, which the default fit set does.
ablation_iep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  m <- model_comparison[model_comparison$scoring == sc, ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(list(
    c("item:evaluator:prompt",      "f2_complete",       "f2_additive"),
    c("item:evaluator:prompt:temp", "f2_complete_drift", "f2_complete")), function(p) {
    a <- m[m$spec == p[2], ]
    b <- m[m$spec == p[3], ]
    if (nrow(a) != 1L || nrow(b) != 1L) return(NULL)
    data.frame(dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, term = p[1],
               bic_estimator = COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR,
               spec_with = p[2], spec_without = p[3],
               BIC_with = a$BIC, BIC_without = b$BIC, delta_BIC = b$BIC - a$BIC,
               both_converged = isTRUE(a$converged) && isTRUE(b$converged),
               row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
if (is.null(ablation_iep) || !nrow(ablation_iep)) {
  ablation_iep <- NULL
  cat("ablation not available: the Family 2 specifications must all be fitted
")
} else {
  knitr::kable(ablation_iep, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = sprintf("%s BIC change from omitting each item-side term of Family 2 in turn, per scoring; positive favours keeping the term.", COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR))
}
