5 Refit f2_complete_drift with REML

f2_complete_drift is refitted under REML for both scorings. It supplies the reported variance components, coefficients, Wald intervals, and D-study projections.

# Relative error collects item-involving components, each divided by the levels
# of the non-object facets it involves; absolute error adds the non-item
# components on the same convention.
#
# This is written generically over component names rather than against a fixed
# list of terms, because the model family below ranges from main effects only
# to the saturated specification and every member needs the same functional.
# "Residual" is the five-way term: with one observation per cell,
# item:evaluator:prompt:temp:seed is confounded with residual error, so it
# enters relative error divided by all four instrumentation facets.
FACET_KEY <- c(evaluator = "e", prompt = "p", temp = "t", seed = "s")

gcoef_from_vec <- function(v, n) {
  nlev <- c(e = n$e, p = n$p, t = n$t, s = n$s)
  tau <- 0; rel <- 0; abso <- 0
  for (i in seq_along(v)) {
    val   <- v[[i]]
    if (is.na(val)) next
    nm    <- names(v)[i]
    parts <- if (identical(nm, "Residual")) FACETS else strsplit(nm, ":")[[1]]
    others <- setdiff(parts, OBJECT)
    denom  <- if (length(others)) prod(nlev[FACET_KEY[others]]) else 1
    if (OBJECT %in% parts) {
      if (!length(others)) tau <- tau + val
      else { rel <- rel + val / denom; abso <- abso + val / denom }
    } else {
      abso <- abso + val / denom
    }
  }
  c(tau = tau, rel = rel, abs = abso,
    Erho2 = tau / (tau + rel), Phi = tau / (tau + abso))
}
# Delta-method Wald intervals on Erho2 AND Phi from the deviance Hessian,
# following the established convention (V_theta = 2 H^-1, numerical Jacobian). The
# Hessian is the expensive part, so it is computed once per fit and reused for
# both coefficients. Near a variance boundary this Hessian is ill-conditioned;
# the resulting interval can be unreliable, which is why the bootstrap
# intervals below are the primary basis for design comparisons.
wald_ci_both <- function(fit, n) {
  # The fitted objective (REML criterion, or ML deviance), on the scale the
  # delta method needs.
  #
  # lme4's devfun2() returns the ML objective even for a REML fit -- its own
  # documentation says so, and points at getME(fm, "devfun") for the REML
  # criterion.  That function takes theta on the Cholesky scale with sigma
  # profiled out, so it is un-profiled back onto (sd, sigma) here:
  #
  #   REML(theta, sigma) = REML_profiled(theta)
  #                        + (n-p) * (log(sigma^2 / sigmahat^2(theta)) - 1)
  #                        + pwrss(theta) / sigma^2
  #
  # with sigmahat^2(theta) = pwrss(theta) / (n - p).  At sigma = sigmahat the
  # correction is zero, so the function reproduces REMLcrit(fit) at the optimum;
  # that identity is asserted below rather than assumed.
  dv_p  <- lme4::getME(fit, "devfun")
  env   <- environment(dv_p)
  # Reaching into a package closure: name what is expected so a future lme4
  # restructure fails here with a readable message rather than as
  # "attempt to apply non-function" from inside numDeriv.
  if (!is.environment(env) || is.null(env$pp) || is.null(env$resp))
    stop("lme4 devfun environment does not expose pp/resp; wald_ci_both needs updating")
  n_obs <- stats::nobs(fit)
  p_fix <- length(lme4::fixef(fit))
  # Degrees of freedom of the profiled scale: n - p under REML, n under ML.
  n_df  <- if (USE_REML) n_obs - p_fix else n_obs
  dd <- function(par) {
    s   <- par[length(par)]
    rel <- par[-length(par)] / s
    base  <- dv_p(rel)
    pwrss <- env$resp$wrss() + env$pp$sqrL(1)
    base + n_df * (log(s^2 * n_df / pwrss) - 1) + pwrss / s^2
  }
  theta <- c(unname(fit@optinfo$val) * sigma(fit), sigma(fit))
  # The un-profiling must reproduce the fitted criterion exactly at the optimum.
  # If it does not, the curvature below is being taken on the wrong surface.
  crit  <- if (USE_REML) lme4::REMLcrit(fit) else -2 * as.numeric(logLik(fit))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(dd(theta), crit, tolerance = 1e-6)))
  nms   <- c(names(getME(fit, "theta")), "sigma")

  make_f <- function(which) function(th) {
    s2 <- th^2
    v  <- setNames(s2[-length(s2)],
                   sub("\\.\\(Intercept\\)$", "", nms[-length(nms)]))
    v["Residual"] <- s2[length(s2)]
    gcoef_from_vec(v, n)[[which]]
  }
  est <- vapply(c("Erho2", "Phi"), function(w) make_f(w)(theta), numeric(1))

  H  <- tryCatch(numDeriv::hessian(dd, theta), error = function(e) NULL)
  # Near a variance boundary the Hessian comes back with non-finite entries
  # rather than erroring.  solve() then succeeds on garbage and the interval
  # is silently wrong, which is worse than having none.
  if (!is.null(H) && !all(is.finite(H))) H <- NULL
  Vt <- if (is.null(H)) NULL else tryCatch(2 * solve(H), error = function(e) NULL)
  # numDeriv left the fit's pp/resp reference objects at the last perturbed
  # theta; evaluate once more at the optimum so the fit is unchanged afterwards.
  invisible(dd(theta))
  if (is.null(Vt)) {
    return(list(Erho2 = c(est[["Erho2"]], NA, NA),
                Phi   = c(est[["Phi"]],   NA, NA)))
  }
  out <- list()
  for (w in c("Erho2", "Phi")) {
    J  <- numDeriv::grad(make_f(w), theta)
    se <- sqrt(max(as.numeric(t(J) %*% Vt %*% J), 0))
    out[[w]] <- c(est[[w]], est[[w]] - 1.96 * se, est[[w]] + 1.96 * se)
  }
  out
}
# p runs to 5, not 3: the 4x5x1x1 design in the reported set would otherwise sit
# outside the grid the bootstrap projects onto and could carry no interval.
# Only three prompts were run, so n_p > 3 is extrapolation and is flagged as such.
DSTUDY_GRID <- expand.grid(e = 1:8, p = 1:5, t = c(1, 3, 6), s = 1:3)

comp_rows <- list(); g_rows <- list(); ds_rows <- list()

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
# The same reported specification is used for both numerical scorings.
for (est in ESTIMATOR) {
  t0_fit <- Sys.time()
  fit <- lmer(FORMS[[REPORT_SPEC]], data = DS[[sc]], REML = USE_REML, control = CTRL)
  conv_msgs <- fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages; conv_msgs <- conv_msgs[!grepl("singular", conv_msgs, fixed = TRUE)]
  if (!identical(as.integer(fit@optinfo$conv$opt), 0L) || length(conv_msgs))
    stop("reported REML fit: convergence problem -- ", paste(c(if (!identical(as.integer(fit@optinfo$conv$opt), 0L)) "optimizer code != 0", conv_msgs), collapse = "; "))
  secs_fit <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0_fit, units = "secs"))

  vcdf <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
  v    <- setNames(vcdf$vcov, vcdf$grp)
  tot  <- sum(v)

  comp_rows[[length(comp_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, estimator = est, spec = REPORT_SPEC,
    source = names(v), variance = as.numeric(v),
    pct_of_total = 100 * as.numeric(v) / tot,
    # Relative to the total, not an absolute cut on an outcome-scale variance:
    # 1e-10 means something quite different for a 1-7 severity scale than for a
    # 0/1 flag.
    at_boundary = as.numeric(v) < 1e-8 * tot, row.names = NULL)

  g  <- gcoef_from_vec(v, DESIGN)
  ci <- wald_ci_both(fit, DESIGN)
  g_rows[[length(g_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, estimator = est, spec = REPORT_SPEC,
    tau = g[["tau"]], rel_error_var = g[["rel"]], abs_error_var = g[["abs"]],
    Erho2 = g[["Erho2"]], Erho2_lo = ci$Erho2[2], Erho2_hi = ci$Erho2[3],
    Phi = g[["Phi"]], Phi_lo = ci$Phi[2], Phi_hi = ci$Phi[3],
    # Names the interval these endpoints are: the delta-method Wald interval of
    # the refit, retained as a check.  The reported intervals are the item-cluster
    # bootstrap's, exported in dstudy_bootstrap_ci_<dataset>.csv.
    interval_method = "wald_delta",
    total_var = tot, n_boundary = sum(as.numeric(v) < 1e-8 * tot),   # same relative rule as at_boundary,
    singular = isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-5), fit_secs = secs_fit, row.names = NULL)

  cat(sprintf("[%s] %-4s [%s] item = %.4f (%.2f%%)  resid = %.2f%%  Erho2 = %.4f  Phi = %.4f  (%.0f s)\n",
              sc, est, REPORT_SPEC, v[["item"]], 100 * v[["item"]] / tot,
              100 * v[["Residual"]] / tot, g[["Erho2"]], g[["Phi"]], secs_fit))

  # Projections are built from the fitted components, matching the estimator that
  # supplies every other reported number.
  if (identical(est, ESTIMATOR)) {
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(DSTUDY_GRID))) {
      n <- as.list(DSTUDY_GRID[i, ]); names(n) <- c("e", "p", "t", "s")
      gg <- gcoef_from_vec(v, n)
      ds_rows[[length(ds_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, spec = REPORT_SPEC,
        n_e = n$e, n_p = n$p, n_t = n$t, n_s = n$s,
        calls_per_item = n$e * n$p * n$t * n$s,
        # Carried on every projected row, not only the named scenarios: a
        # projection past the observed pool is an extrapolation wherever it
        # appears, and a table that drops the flag reads as if it were not.
        extrapolated = n$e > DESIGN$e | n$p > DESIGN$p,
        Erho2 = gg[["Erho2"]], Phi = gg[["Phi"]], row.names = NULL)
    }
  }
}
}

#> [3L] REML [f2_complete_drift] item = 0.4245 (68.73%)  resid = 14.76%  Erho2 = 0.9668  Phi = 0.9657  (41 s)

components   <- bind_rows(comp_rows)
gcoefficients <- bind_rows(g_rows)
dstudy       <- bind_rows(ds_rows)

# Downstream report-side D-study tables must use the REML refit for the
# reported specification, not the ML comparison vector retained for BIC.
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  cc <- components[components$scoring == sc & components$estimator == ESTIMATOR, ]
  V_BY_SPEC[[sc]][[REPORT_SPEC]] <- setNames(cc$variance, cc$source)
}

5.1 The item component against the ANOVA value

This comparison measures the total difference between the reported REML item component and the full-array ANOVA estimate; it does not separate specification differences from estimator effects. Under ML the equality below does not hold even for interior solutions, because ML shrinks the item and the large interaction components (small components can move either way, as the saved ML/REML comparison shows), so the gap then also carries the ML bias.

For a balanced design the ANOVA estimators coincide with REML wherever the components are non-negative. That is a joint condition, not a per-component one: REML maximises subject to non-negativity across all components at once, so if any component is pinned at the boundary the constrained solution differs from the unconstrained ANOVA solution in the other components too, including the item component this table compares. The signed decomposition above shows the condition does not hold exactly here — some components come out below zero — so the equality holds only approximately, and the size of its failure is not measured here; the truncation shift that section reports is a related quantity, not the same one.

The gap below is therefore model reduction plus an estimator term. Only the truncation shift is computed here; the estimator term itself would need a REML fit of the saturated array, which is not run, so the gap is reported as a whole against the ANOVA reference and the truncation shift is shown beside it as a related, measured quantity rather than as a part of the estimator term. Under ML the two would be confounded as well.

gap <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  m <- COMP[[sc]]$var_truncated[COMP[[sc]]$effect == "item"]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(ESTIMATOR, function(est) {
    v <- components$variance[components$scoring == sc &
                             components$estimator == est &
                             components$source == "item"]
    data.frame(scoring = sc, estimator = est, item_variance = v,
               anova_item = m, abs_diff = abs(v - m),
               pct_of_anova = 100 * abs(v - m) / m, row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
# The estimator term, measured when the saturated specification is fitted.  See the other
# univariate documents: the saturated specification under REML is the same
# estimand as the ANOVA decomposition when the non-negativity constraint is not
# binding, so their difference IS the estimator term.  order4 is that
# specification and is fitted only when max_order = 4.
gap$estimator_term <- NA_real_
gap$reduction_term <- NA_real_
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  if (!"order4" %in% names(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]])) next
  v_sat <- V_BY_SPEC[[sc]][["order4"]][["item"]]
  m_ref <- COMP[[sc]]$var_truncated[COMP[[sc]]$effect == "item"]
  v_rep <- components$variance[components$scoring == sc &
                               components$estimator == ESTIMATOR &
                               components$source == "item"]
  gap$estimator_term[gap$scoring == sc] <- abs(v_sat - m_ref)
  gap$reduction_term[gap$scoring == sc] <- abs(v_rep - v_sat)
  cat(sprintf("[%s] saturated %s vs ANOVA (estimator) : %.3e   reported vs saturated (reduction): %.3e\n",
              sc, ESTIMATOR, abs(v_sat - m_ref), abs(v_rep - v_sat)))
}
if (all(is.na(gap$estimator_term)))
  cat("saturated specification not fitted; the gap is reduction plus an\n",
      "estimator term not measured separately here (the truncation shift above\n",
      "is a related quantity, not a bound on it).  Both hierarchy = TRUE and\n",
      "max_order = 4 are needed to fit it; neither is set to the required value\n",
      "by default, so this is the usual path.\n",
      sep = "")
#> saturated specification not fitted; the gap is reduction plus an
#> estimator term not measured separately here (the truncation shift above
#> is a related quantity, not a bound on it).  Both hierarchy = TRUE and
#> max_order = 4 are needed to fit it; neither is set to the required value
#> by default, so this is the usual path.
knitr::kable(gap, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = paste("Item component against the ANOVA value, both scorings.  When the",
                             "saturated specification is fitted, the gap splits into the",
                             "estimator term (saturated fit vs ANOVA) and the reduction term."))
Item component against the ANOVA value, both scorings. When the saturated specification is fitted, the gap splits into the estimator term (saturated fit vs ANOVA) and the reduction term.
scoring estimator item_variance anova_item abs_diff pct_of_anova estimator_term reduction_term

3L REML 0.424454 0.424722 0.000268 0.063151 NA NA

5.2 What the collapse does to the partition

cmp7 <- gcoefficients[gcoefficients$scoring == "7L" &
                      gcoefficients$estimator == ESTIMATOR, ]
cmp3 <- gcoefficients[gcoefficients$scoring == "3L" &
                      gcoefficients$estimator == ESTIMATOR, ]

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("tau", "relative error", "absolute error", "Erho2", "Phi"),
  `7L` = c(cmp7$tau, cmp7$rel_error_var, cmp7$abs_error_var, cmp7$Erho2, cmp7$Phi),
  `3L` = c(cmp3$tau, cmp3$rel_error_var, cmp3$abs_error_var, cmp3$Erho2, cmp3$Phi),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL),
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Seven-level scoring against the three-level collapse, REML, observed design.")
Seven-level scoring against the three-level collapse, REML, observed design.

#> Erho2 moves -6.203e-03 when the scale is collapsed; Phi moves -6.935e-03

The two scorings are not two datasets — they are the same 21,600 annotations read on a coarser and a finer scale. The variances themselves must change, since the numbers assigned to the labels change. What is informative is whether the ratio does: a reliability coefficient that survives collapsing seven categories into three is not an artefact of the particular severity values, and that is the form the question about the ordinal mapping has to take to be answerable.

5.3 Does the specification matter?

BIC ranks the candidate specifications by fit. Reliability coefficients are also evaluated under REML for every converged specification.

All coefficient and D-study sensitivity rows use REML refits; the BIC columns come from the ML comparison.

The check is run at four designs, not one. Specifications differ in which terms they absorb into the residual, and an absorbed term is divided under projection by every facet rather than by the facets it involves. Collapsing a facet the absorbed term contains widens the disagreement; collapsing one it does not contain narrows it, so the direction depends on where the absorbed mass sits. Evaluating only at \(n_e = 4, n_p = 3, n_t = 6, n_s = 3\) would still report a flattering case, and the maxima below are taken over the grid rather than assumed at a corner.

# range() of an empty vector is c(Inf, -Inf), so diff() gives -Inf plus a
# warning and the summary line prints a number that looks measured.
spread <- function(x) if (length(x) < 2L) NA_real_ else diff(range(x))

STAB_DESIGNS <- list(
  observed   = DESIGN,
  one_temp   = modifyList(DESIGN, list(t = 1)),
  one_eval   = modifyList(DESIGN, list(e = 1)),
  # Seed is varied too: the divisor gap between pooling item x configuration x
  # temperature into the residual and estimating it separately is exactly a
  # factor of n_s, so a stability check that never moves n_s cannot see it.
  one_seed   = modifyList(DESIGN, list(s = 1))
)

stability <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(STAB_DESIGNS), function(dn) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]]), function(mn) {
      b <- model_comparison[model_comparison$scoring == sc &
                            model_comparison$spec == mn, ]
      if (!isTRUE(b$reml_converged)) return(NULL)
      g <- gcoef_from_vec(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]][[mn]], STAB_DESIGNS[[dn]])
      data.frame(dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc,
                 design = dn, spec = mn,
                 n_re_terms = b$n_re_terms, BIC = b$BIC,
                 bic_estimator = COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR, components_estimator = REPORT_ESTIMATOR,
                 is_reported = identical(mn, REPORT_SPEC),
                 reml_converged = b$reml_converged, reml_singular = b$reml_singular,
                 tau = g[["tau"]], Erho2 = g[["Erho2"]], Phi = g[["Phi"]],
                 row.names = NULL)
    }))
  }))
}))

knitr::kable(stability[order(stability$scoring, stability$design, stability$BIC), ],
             digits = 6, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Reported coefficients under every fitted specification, four designs, both scorings.")

# Reported separately.  The hierarchy controls are deliberate under- and
# over-fits: order1 keeps five terms and absorbs nearly everything into the
# residual, so including it inflates the spread by more than an order of
# magnitude and makes the specification choice look decisive when it is not.
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  for (dn in names(STAB_DESIGNS)) {
    s   <- stability[stability$scoring == sc & stability$design == dn, ]
    fam <- s[s$spec %in% FAMILY_SPECS, ]
    ctl <- s[grepl("^order[0-9]+$", s$spec), ]
    cat(sprintf("[%s] %-9s (e=%d p=%d t=%d s=%d)  family models: Erho2 spread %.2e, Phi spread %.2e",
                sc, dn, STAB_DESIGNS[[dn]]$e, STAB_DESIGNS[[dn]]$p,
                STAB_DESIGNS[[dn]]$t, STAB_DESIGNS[[dn]]$s,
                spread(fam$Erho2), spread(fam$Phi)))
    cat(if (nrow(ctl))
          sprintf("   [with hierarchy controls: %.2e]\n", spread(s$Erho2))
        else "\n")
  }
}

5.4 Reporting designs

Ten named budget points are reported rather than a full grid: the eight designs printed in the manuscript’s D-study table plus two budget-matched additions, so every tabulated design is still reported and the rounds are comparable line by line. Up to three specifications are projected onto them per scoring, and the table below names which: the reported one (f2_complete_drift); its Family 2 counterpart (f2_complete), which is projected whether or not it wins BIC; and whichever specification BIC ranks first for that scoring, when that is neither of the other two. They collapse to fewer rows when one specification holds more than one of those roles. None of them is a competing report; they show how much the recommendation would move under the alternative specifications.

Scenarios that call for more evaluators or prompts than were run extrapolate beyond the observed instrumentation pool; they are flagged rather than dropped, since the submitted analysis reported them.

DSTUDY_SCENARIOS <- data.frame(
  # Ten reporting designs: the eight printed in the manuscript's D-study table
  # (`in_manuscript_table`) plus two budget-matched additions, 2x3x3x1 and 4x5x1x1.
  scenario = c("1x1x1x1", "1x3x1x1", "2x1x1x1", "3x2x1x1", "4x3x1x1",
               "4x3x6x3", "2x3x3x1", "6x3x1x1", "4x5x1x1", "8x3x1x1"),
  e = c(1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 2, 6, 4, 8),
  p = c(1, 3, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5, 3),
  t = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, 3, 1, 1, 1),
  s = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  in_manuscript_table = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE,
                          TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$calls_per_item <- with(DSTUDY_SCENARIOS, e * p * t * s)
DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$extrapolated   <- with(DSTUDY_SCENARIOS,
                                        e > DESIGN$e | p > DESIGN$p)

# The grid and the reported scenario set are shared contracts across all five
# documents.  Assert them here rather than trusting five copies to stay equal:
# a document that quietly drops a condition would otherwise produce a table that
# looks complete and is not.
stopifnot(nrow(DSTUDY_GRID) == 360L)
stopifnot(setequal(sort(unique(DSTUDY_GRID$e)), 1:8),
          setequal(sort(unique(DSTUDY_GRID$p)), 1:5),
          setequal(sort(unique(DSTUDY_GRID$t)), c(1, 3, 6)),
          setequal(sort(unique(DSTUDY_GRID$s)), 1:3))
stopifnot(nrow(DSTUDY_SCENARIOS) == 10L)
# Every reported condition must lie in the grid, or it can carry a point
# estimate but never an interval.
stopifnot(all(vapply(seq_len(nrow(DSTUDY_SCENARIOS)), function(i)
  any(DSTUDY_GRID$e == DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$e[i] & DSTUDY_GRID$p == DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$p[i] &
      DSTUDY_GRID$t == DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$t[i] & DSTUDY_GRID$s == DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$s[i]), logical(1))))

# Shape assertions alone would let two documents drift apart while both pass, so
# the shared definition is also fingerprinted.  Any edit to the grid or the
# reported scenario set in ONE file changes its digest and stops that file --
# the five must be updated together or not at all.
.contract <- paste0(
  paste(apply(DSTUDY_GRID[order(DSTUDY_GRID$e, DSTUDY_GRID$p, DSTUDY_GRID$t, DSTUDY_GRID$s), ],
              1, paste, collapse = "-"), collapse = ","), "|",
  paste(apply(DSTUDY_SCENARIOS[order(DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$e, DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$p, DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$t, DSTUDY_SCENARIOS$s),
                       c("e", "p", "t", "s")], 1, paste, collapse = "-"),
        collapse = ","))
stopifnot(identical(unname(tools::md5sum(local({
  f <- tempfile(); writeLines(.contract, f, sep = ""); f
}))), "d5cf1e3e963af712e48620b9b8758352"))



# ELIGIBILITY FOR THE CROSS-FAMILY BIC SENSITIVITY, one rule for all five documents:
# the lowest-BIC specification among every fitted specification that converged,
# excluding the hierarchy controls and legacy benchmarks.  Those specifications
# answer diagnostic questions outside the three instrument-configuration
# families.  The drift sensitivity remains eligible because it tests the
# residual-divisor assumption within the reported family.
# BIC is computed per scoring, so the BIC-best specification is selected per
# scoring too.
# The candidate universe is FIXED: the eleven family specifications.  It does not widen when the benchmark or hierarchy switches are on.
DSTUDY_BIC_BEST <- list()
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  m  <- model_comparison[model_comparison$scoring == sc &
                         model_comparison$converged %in% TRUE, ]
  m  <- m[m$spec %in% BIC_UNIVERSE, ]
  DSTUDY_BIC_BEST[[sc]] <- m$spec[which.min(m$BIC)]
}

# Variance vectors are stored before convergence is judged, so existence in
# V_BY_SPEC is not evidence that a fit converged.  Filter against the
# comparison table, per scoring, and refuse to proceed if the reported specification
# itself did not converge.
CONVERGED_SPECS <- lapply(setNames(SCORINGS, SCORINGS), function(sc)
  model_comparison$spec[model_comparison$scoring == sc &
                         model_comparison$converged %in% TRUE])
for (sc in SCORINGS)
  if (!REPORT_SPEC %in% CONVERGED_SPECS[[sc]])
    stop("the reported specification did not converge for scoring ", sc)

# A specification can hold more than one role: the drift sensitivity is often
# also the BIC-best fit.  Label every role it holds rather than the first.
dstudy_role <- function(mn, sc) {
  # "BIC-best" out of a field of one is not a finding; see the other univariate
  # documents.
  bic_meaningful <- length(FORMS) > 1L
  r <- c(if (identical(mn, REPORT_SPEC)) "reported",
         if (identical(mn, PAIR_SPEC)) PAIR_LABEL,
         if (bic_meaningful && identical(mn, DSTUDY_BIC_BEST[[sc]])) "cross-family BIC-best")
  paste(r, collapse = " + ")
}

DSTUDY_SPECS_OF <- lapply(setNames(SCORINGS, SCORINGS), function(sc) {
  m <- unique(c(REPORT_SPEC, PAIR_SPEC, DSTUDY_BIC_BEST[[sc]]))
  m[m %in% CONVERGED_SPECS[[sc]] & m %in% names(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]])]
})

dstudy_scenarios <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  mods <- DSTUDY_SPECS_OF[[sc]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(mods, function(mn) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(DSTUDY_SCENARIOS)), function(i) {
      s2 <- DSTUDY_SCENARIOS[i, ]
      g  <- gcoef_from_vec(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]][[mn]],
                           list(e = s2$e, p = s2$p, t = s2$t, s = s2$s))
      data.frame(dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, spec = mn,
                 components_estimator = REPORT_ESTIMATOR,
                 role = dstudy_role(mn, sc),
                 scenario = s2$scenario,
                 n_e = s2$e, n_p = s2$p, n_t = s2$t, n_s = s2$s,
                 calls_per_item = s2$calls_per_item,
                 extrapolated = s2$extrapolated,
                 Erho2 = g[["Erho2"]], Phi = g[["Phi"]], row.names = NULL)
    }))
  }))
}))

Each contrast below compares two separate refits, not two parameterisations of one fit, so no exact identity holds between them at any design. There may be one contrast or two: the paired Family 2 contrast is always reported, and a cross-family BIC contrast joins it whenever that specification is distinct. What the design does control is where a difference can be large: a term the reported specification absorbs into the residual is divided under projection by every facet, including seed, while a specification that estimates it separately divides it by the facets it actually involves. Collapsing seed removes that divisor gap, so differences are smallest where \(n_s = 1\) and largest where seed is replicated — but only when the two specifications being contrasted differ solely in how a seed-free component is pooled. When BIC instead selects a specification that estimates additional components in their own right, the two differ everywhere. The observed maxima below are reported without assuming which case applies.

# Tables built inside loops are emitted as markdown so they render as tables.
show_kable <- function(k) cat("", k, "", sep = "\n")
# The named scenarios cannot test whether the reported-versus-drift gap grows
# with seed replication: nine of the ten hold n_s = 1 and the only n_s = 3 row
# also moves n_t from 1 to 6, so seed and temperature are confounded there.
# This holds n_e and n_p fixed and varies n_t and n_s independently.
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  mods <- DSTUDY_SPECS_OF[[sc]]
  if (!(PAIR_SPEC %in% mods)) next
  iso <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 3, 6), function(nt) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(ns) {
      n <- list(e = DESIGN$e, p = DESIGN$p, t = nt, s = ns)
      a <- gcoef_from_vec(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]][[REPORT_SPEC]], n)
      b <- gcoef_from_vec(V_BY_SPEC[[sc]][[PAIR_SPEC]], n)
      data.frame(scoring = sc, n_t = nt, n_s = ns,
                 d_Erho2 = a[["Erho2"]] - b[["Erho2"]], row.names = NULL)
    }))
  }))
  show_kable(knitr::kable(iso, digits = 8, row.names = FALSE,
        caption = sprintf("%s: %s minus %s, n_e and n_p at the observed design.",
                          sc, REPORT_SPEC, PAIR_SPEC)))
}

# Two contrasts per scoring, computed independently: the paired Family 2
# complete-structure contrast and, when distinct, the cross-family BIC
# sensitivity.
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  mods <- DSTUDY_SPECS_OF[[sc]]
  cons <- list()
  if (PAIR_SPEC %in% mods)
    cons[[PAIR_LABEL]] <- PAIR_SPEC
  if (!identical(DSTUDY_BIC_BEST[[sc]], REPORT_SPEC) &&
      !identical(DSTUDY_BIC_BEST[[sc]], PAIR_SPEC) &&
      DSTUDY_BIC_BEST[[sc]] %in% mods)
    cons[["cross-family BIC-best"]] <- DSTUDY_BIC_BEST[[sc]]

  if (!length(cons)) {
    cat(sprintf("%s: no contrast to report.\n", sc)); next
  }
  d <- dstudy_scenarios[dstudy_scenarios$scoring == sc, ]
  for (lab in names(cons)) {
    a <- d[d$spec == REPORT_SPEC, ]
    b <- d[d$spec == cons[[lab]], ]
    stopifnot(identical(a$scenario, b$scenario))
    gap <- data.frame(scenario = a$scenario, n_s = a$n_s,
                      Erho2_reported = a$Erho2, Erho2_other = b$Erho2,
                      d_Erho2 = a$Erho2 - b$Erho2,
                      d_Phi   = a$Phi   - b$Phi, row.names = NULL)
    show_kable(knitr::kable(gap, digits = 8, row.names = FALSE,
          caption = sprintf("%s: reported (%s) minus %s (%s).",
                            sc, REPORT_SPEC, lab, cons[[lab]])))
    for (grp in list(list("n_s = 1", gap$n_s == 1), list("n_s > 1", gap$n_s > 1))) {
      g <- gap[grp[[2]], ]
      if (nrow(g))
        cat(sprintf("%s, %s, scenarios with %s: %d, maximum |difference| in Erho2 %.3e, in Phi %.3e\n\n",
                    sc, lab, grp[[1]], nrow(g), max(abs(g$d_Erho2)), max(abs(g$d_Phi))))
    }
  }
}

6 D-study with bootstrap intervals

Why the projected coefficients carry intervals.

The original analysis reported Wald intervals on the observed-design coefficients only. The design recommendations, however, rest on the projected coefficients, which carried no uncertainty at all. The bootstrap stage attaches intervals to every projection using a nonparametric item-cluster bootstrap of the reported specification.

Items are the object of measurement and the only independently sampled units in the design, so the 100 items are resampled with replacement. The reported specification is refitted on each resample under the reporting estimator and its components are projected onto every design in the grid.

The bootstrap and point estimate therefore use the same report-side constrained estimator. Variance components can lie on the nonnegative boundary, so the bootstrap distribution may pile up at zero; that behaviour is part of the estimator being evaluated rather than removed by truncation after fitting.

It also answers how much the 100-item sample limits the stability of the item-related components: the interval width is that answer, because the resampling unit is the item, not the annotation.

What these intervals do not cover. Only items are resampled, so every interval is conditional on the four evaluators, three prompts, six temperatures and three seeds actually observed. The sampling variability of the instrumentation facets — the evaluator component rests on 3 degrees of freedom — is not represented at all. Two consequences follow. Φ intervals are optimistic, because absolute error depends on the non-item components that carry none of their own uncertainty here. And the rows with n_e > 4 project beyond the observed pool: they are extrapolations under the assumption that further evaluators behave like these four, not interpolations within a sampled universe. The intervals are also conditional on the reported specification: model-selection uncertainty is not resampled, and the stability and scenario tables above are the mitigation.

#' Precompute the structure needed to evaluate Erho2 / Phi quickly over the
#' 360-design grid in the reconcile chunk; the facet membership of each
#' component is resolved once.
make_gfun <- function(effect_names) {
  noobj    <- setdiff(FACETS, OBJECT)
  parts    <- strsplit(effect_names, ":")
  has_item <- vapply(parts, function(p) OBJECT %in% p, logical(1))
  # exponent matrix: how many levels of each non-object facet divide it
  E <- t(vapply(parts, function(p) as.numeric(noobj %in% p),
                numeric(length(noobj))))
  colnames(E) <- noobj
  is_tau <- has_item & (rowSums(E) == 0)

  function(vc, n) {
    v       <- pmax(vc, 0)
    denom   <- exp(E %*% log(as.numeric(n[noobj])))
    contrib <- v / as.numeric(denom)
    tau     <- sum(v[is_tau])
    rel     <- sum(contrib[has_item & !is_tau])
    abso    <- rel + sum(contrib[!has_item])
    c(Erho2 = tau / (tau + rel), Phi = tau / (tau + abso))
  }
}

#' Bias-corrected and accelerated percentile interval.
bca_ci <- function(theta_hat, boots, jacks, alpha = 0.05) {
  # Captured BEFORE filtering.  Taking it from a default argument would be
  # lazily evaluated after the filter and compare the survivors with
  # themselves, which always passes.
  n_jack_expected <- length(jacks)
  boots <- boots[is.finite(boots)]
  # The jackknife is filtered too.  Under model refits a single failed leave-one-
  # out fit is realistic, and an unfiltered NA propagates through mean(jacks)
  # into the acceleration constant, turning an otherwise good interval into NA.
  jacks <- jacks[is.finite(jacks)]
  # The acceleration constant is a skewness estimate over leave-one-out
  # replicates.  Two of them cannot carry that, so the floor is a proportion of
  # what the jackknife should have produced, not a token count: losing a fifth
  # of the items means the interval is reported on a different design than the
  # one claimed, and NA is the honest answer.
  if (length(boots) < 50 ||
      length(jacks) < max(2L, ceiling(0.8 * n_jack_expected)))
    return(c(lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, q_lo = NA_real_, q_hi = NA_real_, n_lo = NA_real_, n_hi = NA_real_))
  # Mid-p bias correction: replicates tied with the estimate count as half
  # below.  Without it a boundary estimate, where many replicates equal it
  # exactly, collapses the interval onto that value.
  p0  <- mean(boots < theta_hat) + 0.5 * mean(boots == theta_hat)
  z0  <- qnorm(min(max(p0, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))
  jm  <- mean(jacks)
  den <- 6 * (sum((jm - jacks)^2)^1.5)
  a   <- if (den > 0) sum((jm - jacks)^3) / den else 0
  adj <- vapply(c(alpha / 2, 1 - alpha / 2), function(p) {
    zq  <- qnorm(p)
    dnm <- 1 - a * (z0 + zq)
    # The BCa map is singular where the acceleration term reaches 1 and flips
    # sides beyond it; neither yields an interval, so the level becomes NA.
    if (!is.finite(dnm) || dnm <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    min(max(pnorm(z0 + (z0 + zq) / dnm), 1e-4), 1 - 1e-4)
  }, numeric(1))
  # Reversed or undefined levels are not an interval: report NA and let the
  # caller fall back on the percentile interval it prints alongside.
  if (anyNA(adj) || adj[1] >= adj[2])
    return(c(lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, q_lo = NA_real_, q_hi = NA_real_, n_lo = NA_real_, n_hi = NA_real_))
  qs <- as.numeric(quantile(boots, adj, names = FALSE))
  # The adjusted quantile levels and the number of replicates beyond each
  # endpoint travel with the interval.  An endpoint that rests on a handful of
  # replicates is a Monte Carlo statement about the tail of B draws, not about
  # the estimand; callers flag those and print the percentile interval beside it.
  c(lo = qs[1], hi = qs[2], q_lo = adj[1], q_hi = adj[2],
    n_lo = sum(boots < qs[1]), n_hi = sum(boots > qs[2]))
}

#' Percentile interval, used for the variance components.  A component estimate
#' can sit on the boundary or outside the range of its item-resampling
#' distribution, and there the BCa bias correction is not estimable from B
#' replicates: the interval collapses to a point, which reads as certainty.
#' `bca_ci()` remains the interval for the coefficients, whose estimates are
#' interior.
pct_ci <- function(boots, alpha = 0.05) {
  boots <- boots[is.finite(boots)]
  if (length(boots) < 50) return(c(lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_))
  q <- quantile(boots, c(alpha / 2, 1 - alpha / 2), names = FALSE)
  c(lo = q[1], hi = q[2])
}

Three implementations of the same functional appear in this document, each with its own input convention: g_coefficients() over the method-of-moments basis, gcoef_from_vec() over lme4 component names, and the closure from make_gfun() built for speed over the projection grid. They are only useful if they agree, so that is asserted rather than assumed.

n_noobj  <- DSIZE[setdiff(FACETS, OBJECT)]
nv_check <- c(evaluator = DESIGN$e, prompt = DESIGN$p,
              temp = DESIGN$t, seed = DESIGN$s)

# Checked for EVERY scoring, not for whichever one a loop happened to leave
# behind in `vc`.  An assertion that silently covers half the document is worse
# than none, because it reads as though it covered all of it.
agree_rows <- list(); worst <- 0
for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  v  <- VC[[sc]]
  a  <- g_coefficients(v, n_noobj, truncate = TRUE)[c("Erho2", "Phi")]
  b  <- make_gfun(names(v))(v, nv_check)
  cc <- gcoef_from_vec(setNames(pmax(as.numeric(v), 0), names(v)),
                       DESIGN)[c("Erho2", "Phi")]
  stopifnot(max(abs(a - b)) < 1e-12, max(abs(a - cc)) < 1e-12)
  worst <- max(worst, abs(a - b), abs(a - cc))
  agree_rows[[sc]] <- data.frame(
    scoring = sc,
    implementation = c("g_coefficients", "make_gfun", "gcoef_from_vec"),
    Erho2 = c(a[["Erho2"]], b[["Erho2"]], cc[["Erho2"]]),
    Phi   = c(a[["Phi"]],   b[["Phi"]],   cc[["Phi"]]), row.names = NULL)
}

BOOT_ENGINE <- tolower(REPORT_ESTIMATOR)   # bootstrap refits use the reporting estimator
# A hard-coded core count is a portability bug: 14 workers on a 2-core runtime
# thrash, and each lme4 worker holds its own copy of the data.  0 = detect.
BOOT_CORES <- if (isTRUE(params$boot_cores > 0)) {
  as.integer(params$boot_cores)
} else {
  # detectCores() returns NA on some platforms; max(1L, NA - 2L) is NA, and the
  # `if (BOOT_CORES > 1L)` test below then errors instead of falling back.
  nc <- suppressWarnings(parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE))
  if (!is.finite(nc)) 1L else max(1L, as.integer(nc) - 2L)
}
# mclapply forks, so it is serial on Windows whatever this says.  Stated rather
# than discovered from a run that takes many times the budgeted wall clock.
if (.Platform$OS.type != "unix" && BOOT_CORES > 1L) {
  cat("note: mclapply is fork-based; running serially on this platform\n")
  BOOT_CORES <- 1L
}

# ---- replicate cache -------------------------------------------------------
# The bootstrap is the only expensive part of this document.  Its replicate
# matrices are written to out_dir with a fingerprint (data, specification set,
# seed, B, reported specification, engine) so that a re-render for wording or
# layout can reload them (params$reuse_bootstrap = TRUE) instead of refitting
# for hours.  A cache whose fingerprint does not match is ignored, not trusted.
boot_cache_path <- function(key) file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("boot_cache_%s.rds", key))
CACHE_VERSION <- "2026-09-05.1"   # bump whenever the statistic layout or the bootstrap computation changes
boot_cache_fp <- function(key) list(key = key, version = CACHE_VERSION, data_md5 = DATA_MD5, spec_md5 = SPEC_MD5,
                                    seed = params$seed, B = B_BOOT, spec = REPORT_SPEC,
                                    engine = BOOT_ENGINE)
# Computation settings that the fingerprint does not name but that would change
# the replicates: optimizer budget, the per-refit time limit, the software
# versions, and the shape of the statistic the replicates hold.  They are stored
# beside the fingerprint and compared on reload; a mismatch recomputes.  A cache
# written before this record existed carries no settings and is recomputed, as
# is one whose fingerprint (including the computation version) has changed.
boot_cache_settings <- function(value) list(
  maxfun = CTRL$optCtrl$maxfun, refit_time_limit = params$refit_time_limit,
  r_version = R.version.string, lme4_version = as.character(packageVersion("lme4")),
  dims = if (is.matrix(value)) dim(value) else if (is.list(value) && is.matrix(value$boot)) c(dim(value$boot), if (is.null(value$jack)) c(0L, 0L) else dim(value$jack)) else NULL,
  colnames = if (is.matrix(value)) colnames(value) else if (is.list(value) && is.matrix(value$boot)) colnames(value$boot) else NULL)
boot_cache_load <- function(key) {
  if (!isTRUE(params$reuse_bootstrap)) return(NULL)
  p <- boot_cache_path(key)
  if (!file.exists(p)) { cat(sprintf("bootstrap cache for '%s': none at %s\n", key, basename(p))); return(NULL) }
  x <- readRDS(p)
  if (!identical(x$fp, boot_cache_fp(key))) {
    cat(sprintf("bootstrap cache for '%s': fingerprint mismatch, recomputing\n", key)); return(NULL)
  }
  want <- boot_cache_settings(x$value)
  if (is.null(x$settings)) {
    cat(sprintf("bootstrap cache for '%s': has no settings record, recomputing\n", key)); return(NULL)
  } else if (!identical(x$settings[c("maxfun", "refit_time_limit", "dims", "colnames")], want[c("maxfun", "refit_time_limit", "dims", "colnames")])) {
    cat(sprintf("bootstrap cache for '%s': settings or shape changed, recomputing\n", key)); return(NULL)
  } else if (!identical(x$settings[c("r_version", "lme4_version")], want[c("r_version", "lme4_version")])) {
    cat(sprintf("bootstrap cache for '%s': WARNING -- computed under %s / lme4 %s, now %s / lme4 %s; reused\n", key,
                x$settings$r_version, x$settings$lme4_version, want$r_version, want$lme4_version))
  }
  cat(sprintf("bootstrap cache for '%s': loaded %s (written %s)\n", key, basename(p),
              format(file.mtime(p), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")))
  x$value
}
boot_cache_save <- function(key, value) {
  if (is.null(value)) return(invisible(NULL))
  saveRDS(list(fp = boot_cache_fp(key), settings = boot_cache_settings(value), value = value), boot_cache_path(key))
  invisible(NULL)
}


#' Replace killed-worker results with NA rows of the right width.
#'
#' mclapply() returns a `try-error` object for a worker the OS killed (OOM is
#' the realistic case here).  rbind()-ing that with numeric vectors yields a
#' ragged or character matrix and the whole bootstrap is silently corrupted
#' rather than failing.  Turn each casualty into an all-NA row instead: the
#' downstream filters already drop non-finite replicates and B_effective
#' already records how many survived.
drop_dead <- function(x, n_quant) {
  bad <- !vapply(x, function(z) is.numeric(z) && length(z) == n_quant, logical(1))
  if (any(bad)) {
    cat(sprintf("note: %d of %d replicates failed or were killed; recorded as NA\n",
                sum(bad), length(x)))
    nm <- NULL
    ok <- which(!bad)
    if (length(ok)) nm <- names(x[[ok[1]]])
    x[bad] <- list(setNames(rep(NA_real_, n_quant), nm))
  }
  x
}
BOOT_GRID   <- DSTUDY_GRID            # same grid as the model-based D-study

n_items <- dim(ARR[[1]])[1]

# Duplicated items MUST be relabelled.  Resampling with replacement and leaving
# the original identifiers in place makes lme4 collapse repeated draws into
# their original factor levels, pulling each replicate toward the original
# sample and understating the interval.
resample_frame <- function(dd, idx_by_item, pick) {
  b <- dd[unlist(idx_by_item[pick], use.names = FALSE), ]
  b$item <- factor(rep(seq_along(pick), times = lengths(idx_by_item[pick])))
  b
}

# A returned lmer object can still carry an optimizer warning. Such a refit is
# treated as failed so it cannot enter the bootstrap distribution.
bootstrap_fit_ok <- function(fit) {
  msgs <- unlist(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages)
  msgs <- msgs[!grepl("singular", msgs, fixed = TRUE)]
  isTRUE(fit@optinfo$conv$opt == 0L) && !length(msgs)
}

#' Erho2 and Phi at every projected design, from one refit of the scoring's
#' reported specification on a resampled dataset.
# Component slots come from the observed-data fit of the reported specification, so
# every replicate returns the same layout regardless of scoring.
COMP_NAMES <- sort(unique(components$source[components$estimator == ESTIMATOR]))
N_QUANT <- 2 * nrow(BOOT_GRID) + length(COMP_NAMES)

stat_reml <- function(pick, sc, idx_by_item) {
  # A refit that exceeds the time limit is a failed replicate (NA row), so one
  # pathological resample cannot stall a worker for the rest of the run.
  fit <- try({
    setTimeLimit(elapsed = params$refit_time_limit, transient = TRUE)
    lmer(FORMS[[REPORT_SPEC]], data = resample_frame(DS[[sc]], idx_by_item, pick),
         REML = USE_REML, control = CTRL)
  }, silent = TRUE)
  setTimeLimit(elapsed = Inf)
  if (inherits(fit, "try-error") || !bootstrap_fit_ok(fit))
    return(rep(NA_real_, N_QUANT))  # unnamed, as the success path is; indexed by position
  vd <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
  v  <- setNames(vd$vcov, vd$grp)
  coefs <- as.numeric(vapply(seq_len(nrow(BOOT_GRID)), function(k) {
    n <- as.list(BOOT_GRID[k, ]); names(n) <- c("e", "p", "t", "s")
    g <- gcoef_from_vec(v, n); c(g[["Erho2"]], g[["Phi"]])
  }, numeric(2)))
  comps <- vapply(COMP_NAMES, function(nm) if (is.na(v[nm])) NA_real_ else v[[nm]],
                  numeric(1))
  c(coefs, unname(comps))
}

STAT <- stat_reml
boot_rows <- list(); comp_ci_rows <- list()

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  idx_by_item <- split(seq_len(nrow(DS[[sc]])), DS[[sc]]$item)
  item_ids    <- names(idx_by_item)

  # Both scorings are seeded identically, so they resample the SAME items in
  # the same order.  The two sets of intervals are then differences in scoring,
  # not differences in which items happened to be drawn.
  set.seed(params$seed)
  picks <- lapply(seq_len(max(B_BOOT, 0L)),
                  function(b) sample(item_ids, n_items, replace = TRUE))

  BR <- boot_cache_load(sprintf("main_%s", sc))
  if (!is.null(BR) && (nrow(BR$boot) != B_BOOT || ncol(BR$boot) != N_QUANT)) { cat("bootstrap cache: replicate or column count does not match this document, recomputing\n"); BR <- NULL }
  if (!is.null(BR) && B_BOOT >= 50 && (is.null(BR$jack) || nrow(BR$jack) != n_items || ncol(BR$jack) != N_QUANT || !identical(colnames(BR$jack), colnames(BR$boot)))) { cat("bootstrap cache: jackknife layout does not match the item count or the statistic layout, recomputing\n"); BR <- NULL }
  BOOT_REUSED[[sprintf("main_%s", sc)]] <- !is.null(BR)
  if (is.null(BR) && B_BOOT >= 1) {
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    boot <- if (BOOT_CORES > 1L) {
      do.call(rbind, drop_dead(parallel::mclapply(picks, STAT, sc = sc,
                                        idx_by_item = idx_by_item,
                                        mc.cores = BOOT_CORES, mc.preschedule = FALSE), N_QUANT))
    } else {
      do.call(rbind, drop_dead(lapply(picks, STAT, sc = sc, idx_by_item = idx_by_item), N_QUANT))
    }
    mins <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))

    # BCa needs a jackknife for the acceleration constant, and enough replicates
    # to be meaningful at all.  Below that it is skipped rather than faked.
    jack <- NULL
    if (B_BOOT >= 50) {
      jp <- lapply(seq_len(n_items), function(i) item_ids[-i])
      jack <- if (BOOT_CORES > 1L) {
        do.call(rbind, drop_dead(parallel::mclapply(jp, STAT, sc = sc,
                                          idx_by_item = idx_by_item,
                                          mc.cores = BOOT_CORES, mc.preschedule = FALSE), N_QUANT))
      } else {
        do.call(rbind, drop_dead(lapply(jp, STAT, sc = sc, idx_by_item = idx_by_item), N_QUANT))
      }
    }
    BR <- list(boot = boot, jack = jack, mins = mins,
               failed = sum(!stats::complete.cases(boot)),
               # The nominal B is what was asked for; these are what BCa
               # actually had to work with.  A run that lost most of its
               # refits should not report an interval as if it had B of them.
               B_effective    = sum(stats::complete.cases(boot)),
               jack_effective = if (is.null(jack)) 0L
                                else sum(stats::complete.cases(jack)))
    cat(sprintf("[%s] engine = %s, B = %d, %d cores, %.1f min, %d failed\n",
                sc, BOOT_ENGINE, B_BOOT, BOOT_CORES, mins, BR$failed))
    if (is.null(jack))
      cat(sprintf("[%s] B < 50: no jackknife, so no BCa interval -- NA by design\n", sc))
    boot_cache_save(sprintf("main_%s", sc), BR)
  } else if (is.null(BR)) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] bootstrap skipped (B_boot < 1)\n", sc))
  }

  # Point estimates come from the scoring's reported specification, the same fit the
  # components table reports.
  ds_sc <- dstudy[dstudy$scoring == sc, ]
  B_EFFECTIVE <- if (is.null(BR)) 0L else BR$B_effective
  JACK_EFFECTIVE <- if (is.null(BR)) 0L else BR$jack_effective
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(BOOT_GRID))) {
    n  <- as.list(BOOT_GRID[k, ]); names(n) <- c("e", "p", "t", "s")
    r  <- ds_sc[ds_sc$n_e == n$e & ds_sc$n_p == n$p &
                ds_sc$n_t == n$t & ds_sc$n_s == n$s, ]
    ie <- 2 * k - 1; ip <- 2 * k
    ci_e <- ci_p <- c(lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, q_lo = NA_real_, q_hi = NA_real_, n_lo = NA_real_, n_hi = NA_real_)
    if (!is.null(BR) && !is.null(BR$jack)) {
      ci_e <- bca_ci(r$Erho2[1], BR$boot[, ie], BR$jack[, ie])
      ci_p <- bca_ci(r$Phi[1],   BR$boot[, ip], BR$jack[, ip])
    }
    pe <- if (!is.null(BR)) pct_ci(BR$boot[, ie]) else c(lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_)
    pp <- if (!is.null(BR)) pct_ci(BR$boot[, ip]) else c(lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_)
    boot_rows[[length(boot_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, spec = REPORT_SPEC,
      engine = BOOT_ENGINE, B = B_BOOT,
      B_effective = B_EFFECTIVE, jack_effective = JACK_EFFECTIVE,
      n_e = n$e, n_p = n$p, n_t = n$t, n_s = n$s,
      calls_per_item = n$e * n$p * n$t * n$s,
      extrapolated = n$e > DESIGN$e | n$p > DESIGN$p,
      Erho2 = r$Erho2[1], Erho2_lo = ci_e[["lo"]], Erho2_hi = ci_e[["hi"]],
      Erho2_width = ci_e[["hi"]] - ci_e[["lo"]],
      Phi = r$Phi[1], Phi_lo = ci_p[["lo"]], Phi_hi = ci_p[["hi"]],
      Phi_width = ci_p[["hi"]] - ci_p[["lo"]],
    Erho2_q_lo = ci_e[["q_lo"]], Erho2_q_hi = ci_e[["q_hi"]],
    Erho2_tail_lo = ci_e[["n_lo"]], Erho2_tail_hi = ci_e[["n_hi"]],
    Phi_q_lo = ci_p[["q_lo"]], Phi_q_hi = ci_p[["q_hi"]],
    Phi_tail_lo = ci_p[["n_lo"]], Phi_tail_hi = ci_p[["n_hi"]],
    Erho2_pct_lo = pe[["lo"]], Erho2_pct_hi = pe[["hi"]],
    Phi_pct_lo = pp[["lo"]], Phi_pct_hi = pp[["hi"]], row.names = NULL)
  }
  # ---- component intervals for this scoring --------------------------------
  # Same resamples that produced the coefficient intervals, so no extra fits.
  # This is what makes `at_boundary` interrogable: a component pinned at zero
  # whose interval hugs zero is genuinely absent, whereas one pinned at zero
  # with a wide interval is simply not estimable at this design.  Percentile
# rather than BCa here; see pct_ci().
  if (!is.null(BR) && !is.null(BR$jack) && length(COMP_NAMES)) {
    off <- 2 * nrow(BOOT_GRID)
    for (m in seq_along(COMP_NAMES)) {
      hat_m <- components$variance[components$scoring == sc &
                                   components$estimator == ESTIMATOR &
                                   components$source == COMP_NAMES[m]][1]
      ci <- pct_ci(BR$boot[, off + m])
      comp_ci_rows[[length(comp_ci_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        scoring = sc, source = COMP_NAMES[m],
        variance_lo = ci[["lo"]], variance_hi = ci[["hi"]],
        covers_zero = if (is.na(ci[["lo"]]) || is.na(ci[["hi"]])) NA else (ci[["lo"]] <= 0 && ci[["hi"]] >= 0),
        row.names = NULL)
    }
  }
}
#> [7L] engine = reml, B = 1000, 14 cores, 57.5 min, 0 failed
#> [3L] engine = reml, B = 1000, 14 cores, 56.6 min, 0 failed
dstudy_bootstrap <- do.call(rbind, boot_rows)

if (length(comp_ci_rows)) {
  components <- merge(components, do.call(rbind, comp_ci_rows),
                      by = c("scoring", "source"), all.x = TRUE)
  shown <- components[components$estimator == ESTIMATOR,
                      c("scoring","source","variance","pct_of_total",
                        "at_boundary","variance_lo","variance_hi","covers_zero")]
  for (cc in c("variance", "variance_lo", "variance_hi")) shown[[cc]] <- sprintf("%.3e", shown[[cc]])
  knitr::kable(shown, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = paste("Variance components with item-cluster percentile intervals, both scorings",
                               "(scientific notation; covers_zero tests the interval, not the printed rounding)."))
} else {
  components$variance_lo <- NA_real_
  components$variance_hi <- NA_real_
  components$covers_zero <- NA
  cat("no component intervals (bootstrap absent or B < 50)\n")
}

# Each coefficient gets its own table, so a design flagged only for Phi shows
# the Phi diagnostics that flagged it rather than an unremarkable Erho2 row.
thin_table <- function(rows, w) {
  cols <- c(intersect(c("scoring", "n_e", "n_p", "n_t", "n_s"), names(rows)),
            w, paste0(w, c("_lo", "_hi", "_q_lo", "_q_hi", "_tail_lo", "_tail_hi", "_pct_lo", "_pct_hi")))
  knitr::kable(rows[, cols], digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = sprintf("Thin-tailed BCa endpoints for %s: adjusted quantile levels, replicates beyond each endpoint, and the percentile interval for comparison.", w))
}
cat(sprintf("  flagged by Erho2: %d; flagged by Phi: %d\n", sum(thin_e), sum(thin_p)))
#>   flagged by Erho2: 0; flagged by Phi: 0
if (any(thin_e)) thin_table(dstudy_bootstrap[thin_e, ], "Erho2")
if (any(thin_p)) thin_table(dstudy_bootstrap[thin_p, ], "Phi")
# Designs where the BCa adjustment is unavailable (singular or reversed map, or
# too few replicates) are listed with their percentile intervals so they are
# never silent.
unavail <- dstudy_bootstrap[is.na(dstudy_bootstrap$Erho2_lo) | is.na(dstudy_bootstrap$Phi_lo), ]
cat(sprintf("Designs where a BCa interval is unavailable: %d of %d\n", nrow(unavail), nrow(dstudy_bootstrap)))
#> Designs where a BCa interval is unavailable: 0 of 720
if (nrow(unavail)) knitr::kable(unavail[, intersect(c("scoring", "n_e", "n_p", "n_t", "n_s", "Erho2", "Erho2_pct_lo", "Erho2_pct_hi", "Phi", "Phi_pct_lo", "Phi_pct_hi"), names(unavail))],

6.1 The reported specification against the saturated decomposition

The bootstrap above resamples and refits the reported specification, so its intervals and the point estimates use the same reporting estimator and there is nothing to reconcile between them. What remains worth measuring is a structural difference: the reported specification does not name several item interactions, and the fit redistributes their variance, mostly into the residual and partly into the retained terms that contain them (item x configuration x temperature, whose divisor excludes seed, takes the item x temperature family); the residual’s share is then divided under projection by \(n_e n_p n_t n_s\), whereas the full 31-component decomposition divides each component by only the facets it involves. That redistribution is a property of the fit, not an exact bookkeeping identity, which is why the gap is measured below rather than derived.

recon <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  gf <- make_gfun(names(VC[[sc]]))
  ds_sc <- dstudy[dstudy$scoring == sc, ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(DSTUDY_GRID)), function(k) {
    n  <- as.list(DSTUDY_GRID[k, ]); names(n) <- c("e", "p", "t", "s")
    nv <- c(evaluator = n$e, prompt = n$p, temp = n$t, seed = n$s)
    mm <- gf(VC[[sc]], nv)
    md <- ds_sc[ds_sc$n_e == n$e & ds_sc$n_p == n$p &
                ds_sc$n_t == n$t & ds_sc$n_s == n$s, ]
    data.frame(dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, spec = REPORT_SPEC,
               n_e = n$e, n_p = n$p, n_t = n$t, n_s = n$s,
               Erho2_model = md$Erho2[1], Erho2_saturated = mm[["Erho2"]],
               Phi_model   = md$Phi[1],   Phi_saturated   = mm[["Phi"]],
               row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
recon$d_Erho2 <- recon$Erho2_model - recon$Erho2_saturated
recon$d_Phi   <- recon$Phi_model   - recon$Phi_saturated

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  r  <- recon[recon$scoring == sc, ]
  at <- r$n_e == 4 & r$n_p == 3 & r$n_t == 6 & r$n_s == 3
  cat(sprintf("[%s] %d designs;  max |model - saturated|: Erho2 %.3e, Phi %.3e;",
              sc, nrow(r), max(abs(r$d_Erho2)), max(abs(r$d_Phi))))
  cat(sprintf("  at observed design: Erho2 %.3e, Phi %.3e\n",
              r$d_Erho2[at], r$d_Phi[at]))
}

#> [3L] 360 designs;  max |model - saturated|: Erho2 7.374e-03, Phi 1.099e-02;  at observed design: Erho2 1.236e-04, Phi 1.999e-04

worst <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  r <- recon[recon$scoring == sc, ]; head(r[order(-abs(r$d_Erho2)), ], 5)
}))

7 Facet severity with item-clustered inference

The cumulative logit models in the original analysis treated all 21,600 rows as independent, but they are 216 repeated evaluations of each of 100 items. Independence is violated at the item level, so the reported standard errors do not reflect that dependence. The direction of the error depends on the facet: where the item-by-facet interaction is large the clustered standard errors are larger than the naive ones, and where it is negligible they can be smaller. Calling the tests “over-powered” settles neither case.

The coefficients themselves are unaffected and reproduce the original values exactly. What changes is their uncertainty, re-estimated here by resampling the 100 items with replacement and refitting — the same item-cluster bootstrap used above. The ratio of clustered to naive standard errors quantifies how much the original inference understated uncertainty.

FORM <- sev ~ evaluator + prompt + temp
sev_rows <- list()

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  set.seed(params$seed)

  ds <- DS[[sc]]
  ds$sev       <- factor(ds$score, ordered = TRUE)
  # Reference levels are set only when the dataset actually has them.  A hard
  # relevel() errors on a corpus that labels its evaluators differently, which
  # turns a cosmetic choice into a failed document.
  ref_if <- function(f, lev) { f <- factor(f); if (lev %in% levels(f)) relevel(f, lev) else f }
  ds$evaluator <- ref_if(ds$evaluator, "gpt-4o-mini")
  ds$prompt    <- ref_if(ds$prompt, "rubric")
  ds$temp      <- ref_if(ds$temp, "0")

  fit_sev  <- polr(FORM, data = ds, Hess = TRUE, method = "logistic")
  if (!identical(as.integer(fit_sev$convergence), 0L)) stop("facet-severity model did not converge")
  est      <- coef(fit_sev)
  se_naive <- sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_sev)))[names(est)]

  idx_by_item <- split(seq_len(nrow(ds)), ds$item)
  items <- names(idx_by_item)

  t0 <- Sys.time()
  # Draws are made in the parent before forking, so the resamples do not depend
  # on the core count; the refits then run in parallel like the REML bootstrap.
  picks_sev <- lapply(seq_len(B_BOOT), function(b) sample(items, length(items), replace = TRUE))
  one_sev <- function(pick) {
    rid <- unlist(idx_by_item[pick], use.names = FALSE)
    fb  <- try(polr(FORM, data = ds[rid, ], Hess = FALSE, method = "logistic"), silent = TRUE)
    out <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(est)), names(est))
    if (!inherits(fb, "try-error") && identical(as.integer(fb$convergence), 0L)) { cb <- coef(fb); out[names(cb)] <- cb }
    out
  }
  bs <- boot_cache_load(sprintf("severity_%s", sc))
  if (!is.null(bs) && (nrow(bs) != B_BOOT || !identical(colnames(bs), names(est)))) { cat("severity cache: coefficient names do not match, recomputing\n"); bs <- NULL }
  if (!is.null(bs) && is.null(attr(bs, "n_nonconverged"))) { cat("severity cache predates the convergence check, recomputing\n"); bs <- NULL }
  SEV_REUSED[[sprintf("severity_%s", sc)]] <- !is.null(bs)
  if (is.null(bs)) {
    sev_list <- if (BOOT_CORES > 1L) {
      parallel::mclapply(picks_sev, one_sev, mc.cores = BOOT_CORES, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
    } else {
      lapply(picks_sev, one_sev)
    }
    bs <- do.call(rbind, drop_dead(sev_list, length(est)))
    attr(bs, "n_nonconverged") <- sum(!stats::complete.cases(bs))   # convergence metadata travels with the cache
    boot_cache_save(sprintf("severity_%s", sc), bs)
  }
  colnames(bs) <- names(est)
  cat(sprintf("[%s] %d bootstraps in %.0fs (%d failed)\n", sc, B_BOOT,
              as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")),
              sum(!complete.cases(bs))))

  # As for the main bootstrap, clustered inference needs enough successful refits:
  # below SEV_MIN_B usable draws the clustered SE, its p-value, and the percentile
  # interval are withheld (NA) rather than computed from a handful of draws.
  # B_effective records how many refits succeeded either way.
  SEV_MIN_B <- 50L
  for (k in names(est)) {
    v <- bs[, k]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    enough <- length(v) >= SEV_MIN_B
    se_cl <- if (enough) sd(v) else NA_real_
    ci    <- if (enough) quantile(v, c(.025, .975), names = FALSE)
             else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    sev_rows[[length(sev_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, term = k, coef = est[[k]],
      B = B_BOOT, B_effective = length(v), jack_effective = NA_integer_,
      se_naive = se_naive[[k]],
      p_naive = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est[[k]] / se_naive[[k]])),
      # Reported alongside p_naive so the comparison below is like-for-like: a
      # p-value from the model's own standard error against an interval from the
      # item-cluster bootstrap compares two different inferential frameworks.
      p_cluster = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est[[k]] / se_cl)),
      se_cluster = se_cl, se_ratio = se_cl / se_naive[[k]],
      ci_lo = ci[1], ci_hi = ci[2],
      crosses_zero = (ci[1] <= 0 && ci[2] >= 0), row.names = NULL)
  }
}
#> [7L] 1000 bootstraps in 31s (0 failed)
#> [3L] 1000 bootstraps in 35s (0 failed)
facet_severity <- do.call(rbind, sev_rows)

knitr::kable(facet_severity, digits = 5, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Facet-severity contrasts, naive vs item-clustered, both scorings.")

for (sc in SCORINGS) {
  f <- facet_severity[facet_severity$scoring == sc, ]
  if (any(f$B_effective < SEV_MIN_B)) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] clustered SE, p-value, and interval withheld: fewer than %d usable replicates (B_effective = %d of %d)\n",
                sc, SEV_MIN_B, min(f$B_effective), B_BOOT))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] median ratio of item-cluster bootstrap SE to naive SE: %.2f (below 1 means the clustered SE is smaller)\n",
                sc, median(f$se_ratio)))
  }
}
#> [7L] median ratio of item-cluster bootstrap SE to naive SE: 0.82 (below 1 means the clustered SE is smaller)
#> [3L] median ratio of item-cluster bootstrap SE to naive SE: 0.91 (below 1 means the clustered SE is smaller)

# The proportional-odds assumption behind polr() is not tested here; these
# contrasts are read as descriptive facet severities, not as a fitted
# cumulative-odds model whose link has been checked.
# Like-for-like: the SAME Wald procedure before and after clustering.  Crossing
# a clustered p-value against a clustered interval compares two clustered
# procedures with each other, which is a numerical curiosity, not the finding
# this section exists to report.  %in% TRUE guards the NA that p_cluster carries
# whenever se_cluster could not be computed.
flip <- facet_severity[(facet_severity$p_naive < 0.05) %in% TRUE &
                       !((facet_severity$p_cluster < 0.05) %in% TRUE), ]
# "not significant after clustering" and "not estimable after clustering" are
# different findings; p_cluster is NA in the second case, so it is shown.
flip$clustered_estimable <- !is.na(flip$p_cluster)
if (nrow(flip)) {
  knitr::kable(flip[, c("scoring", "term", "coef", "p_naive", "p_cluster", "clustered_estimable", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")],
               digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = "Significant by the naive Wald test but not by the clustered Wald test; item-clustered percentile intervals shown alongside.")
} else {
  cat("no term loses significance after clustering, under either scoring\n")
}

8 Outputs

The export tables this stage produced are written to ../../outputs/rmd_ml_select_reml_refit/mental_health as per-dataset slices — the written list below names exactly which, and it is not every table displayed above. Combining the slices across datasets is a separate step and is not performed here.

# Each stage writes what it produced.  The models stage has no intervals, and
# writing an empty or absent table under the same name as a real one is how a
# later reader ends up treating "no bootstrap yet" as "interval was NA".

# Written as one slice per scoring, so the file names match the dataset names
# the combined CSVs use (mental_health_7L, mental_health_3L) and the combiner
# needs no special case for this document.
rows_written <- list()
written <- list(
  mom_components            = comp,
  mom_gcoefficients         = mom_g,
  mom_residual_composition  = resid_comp,
  mom_identity_check        = identity_check,
  uni_model_comparison      = model_comparison,
  uni_specification_stability = stability,
  uni_components            = components[, intersect(names(components),
                                c("dataset", "scoring", "estimator", "spec", "source", "variance", "pct_of_total", "at_boundary"))],
  uni_gcoefficients         = gcoefficients,
  uni_dstudy                = dstudy,
  uni_dstudy_spec_vs_saturated = recon,
  uni_dstudy_scenarios      = dstudy_scenarios,
  # Stamped only when its values were fitted here or came from a verified companion;
  # values inherited from an unstamped file are re-exported unstamped.
  uni_components_by_spec    = if (CB_STATUS %in% c("fitted", "verified"))
                                cbind(components_by_spec, data_md5 = DATA_MD5, spec_md5 = SPEC_MD5,
                                      seed = params$seed, maxfun = CTRL$optCtrl$maxfun) else components_by_spec,
  uni_ablation_iep          = ablation_iep
)
if (identical(params$stage, "bootstrap")) written <- c(written, list(
  dstudy_bootstrap_ci       = dstudy_bootstrap,
  uni_components_with_ci    = components,
  facet_severity_clustered  = facet_severity
))
# The scale and stratum sensitivities are produced in both stages.
written <- c(written, SCALE_TABLES)
# The ML component vectors exist only when the comparison was fitted here.
if (!REUSED) written$uni_components_by_spec_ml <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SCORINGS, function(sc) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(V_BY_SPEC_ML[[sc]]), function(mn) {
    v <- V_BY_SPEC_ML[[sc]][[mn]]
    data.frame(dataset = DATASET_OF[[sc]], scoring = sc, spec = mn, components_estimator = COMPARISON_ESTIMATOR,
               source = names(v), variance = as.numeric(v), row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
# A table this run could not produce (the ablation needs both Family 2
# specifications fitted) is dropped rather than written empty.
written <- Filter(Negate(is.null), written)

# Every slice must be self-identifying.  The combined CSVs are built by stacking
# these files across datasets, and bind_rows() fills missing columns with NA
# rather than failing -- so an unlabelled or ragged slice would corrupt the
# combined table without announcing itself.  Assert instead.
missing_id <- names(written)[!vapply(written, function(x) "dataset" %in% names(x),
                                     logical(1))]
if (length(missing_id)) {
  stop("tables missing a `dataset` column: ", paste(missing_id, collapse = ", "))
}
for (nm in names(written)) {
  tb <- written[[nm]]
  for (sc in SCORINGS) {
    part <- tb[tb$dataset == DATASET_OF[[sc]], , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(part)) next   # a table that belongs to one scoring only
    f <- file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("%s_%s.csv", nm, DATASET_OF[[sc]]))
    write.csv(part, f, row.names = FALSE)
    rows_written[[length(rows_written) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      file = basename(f), rows = nrow(part), row.names = NULL)
  }
}

             caption = "Files written, one slice per scoring.")
